jobs.excerpt: POSITION DESCRIPTIONTHE PEW CHARITABLE TRUSTSSenior Officer, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands (Protected Area Management and Conservation Finance) The Environment Portfolio at The Pew Charitable Trusts For more than 30 years, Pew has been a major force in engaging the public and policy makers about the causes, consequences, and solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges.
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

THE PEW CHARITABLE TRUSTS

Senior Officer, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands

(Protected Area Management and Conservation Finance)

The Environment Portfolio at The Pew Charitable Trusts

For more than 30 years, Pew has been a major force in engaging the public and policy makers about the causes, consequences, and solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Our environment work spans all seven continents with more than 250 professionals working at the local, national, and international levels to reduce the scope and severity of global environmental problems, such as the erosion of large natural ecosystems that contain a great part of the world’s remaining biodiversity, and the destruction of the marine environment. Pew’s global environmental program focuses on science-based, nonpartisan, and sustainable solutions to help protect the planet and people. We work in partnership with governments, Indigenous rights holders, intergovernmental organizations, non-governmental organizations, local stakeholders, scientists, and other researchers to advance public policy so that nature and communities can thrive.

Since 1990, Pew has worked in North America, South America and Australia to protect large and critically important terrestrial ecosystems, including rivers and other freshwater resources, coastal temperate rainforests, interior mountain ranges, the northern boreal forests, Australia’s Outback, and Chilean Patagonia. We work to ensure these natural systems remain bountiful, functioning, and resilient, providing essential ecological services such as clean air and clean water, sustenance and food security for local communities and more broadly for the welfare of current and future generations. Our work relies on the sciences of conservation, sociology, biology, and economics to advocate for practical and durable solutions to the loss of biodiversity.

In the sea, reforms to how our oceans are managed are essential to address overfishing, pollution, and loss of habitat. Pew began its oceans program in the United States, focusing on ending overfishing and protecting fragile marine habitat. Starting in 2005, Pew’s ocean conservation program expanded around the world and played a significant role in reforming marine fisheries management in the European Union and on the high seas and creating large scale marine reserves around the world. Our work is grounded in the best available science and pursues domestic and international conservation measures that are long-term and provide permanent, durable protections for marine ecosystems. We also work to address systemic threats to the ocean, including from plastics, over-and-illegal fishing, seabed mining, and climate change.

Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands

South America’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco regions are among the most ecologically significant tropical wetlands and dry forests on Earth. This area spans parts of Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, and Argentina and contains thousands of plant and animal species and provides vital aquatic habitat, nutrient renewal, migration routes, and flood control for millions of animals and people living downstream. The region’s extensive ecosystems are currently threatened by deforestation, drought and intensification of wildfires related to climate change, and thus urgently need conservation action.

The project works with the policy framework in each country to solidify and expand protection of the extraordinary biodiversity of the Pantanal-Gran Chaco region. Pew partners with local and international conservation organizations, government agencies, and Indigenous governments and organizations to improve management of and expand protected areas, support Indigenous organizations and communities in the management of their territories, promote sustainable management for ranching lands, and to advance long-term conservation financing mechanisms for durable protections.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Project Director, Conserving the Pantanal and Gran Chaco Wildlands, the Senior Officer will lead efforts to develop long-term financing and improve the management of protected and conserved areas in the Pantanal-Gran Chaco landscape.

The Senior Officer will focus on identifying and pursuing finance, conservation, community development, and fundraising goals that support improved management of protected and conserved lands in the region. This will include collaboration with consultants, partners, government officials and other key stakeholders, as well as facilitating the project’s engagement in public policy and advocacy related to conservation finance and improved management. This position requires demonstrated leadership in public or private sector organizations focused on promoting sustainability and conservation.

The Senior Officer will be located either in Santa Cruz, Bolivia; or elsewhere within the South America region following evaluation by Pew.

Responsibilities for the Pantanal-Gran Chaco Project:

  • Foster a work environment that inspires excellence, values impact, encourages transparency, builds mutual trust and respect, embraces and values diversity, and is collaborative, caring and compassionate. Under the Project Director’s leadership, manage aspects of Pew’s Pantanal-Gran Chaco initiative related to improving the management of the region’s protected and conserved areas. This includes organizing and coordinating high-level meetings, commissioning and conducting research, and managing strategic partnerships.
  • In collaboration with relevant Pew staff and senior management, assess opportunities to expand or develop new financing strategies for protected and conserved areas in Bolivia, Brazil, and Argentina.
  • Coordinate the development of priority financing initiatives in collaboration with Pew’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco team, consultants, and in-country partners.
  • Provide technical guidance to Pew’s Pantanal and Gran Chaco team on financing frameworks, sustainable financing mechanisms, public resource allocation, and effective management.
  • Support the Project Director in establishing and cultivating strategic alliances and launching joint initiatives with international organizations, foundations, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), government agencies, Indigenous organizations, and other institutions in the region.
  • Promote best practices and innovations in protected area management and conservation in the Pantanal Gran-Chaco through public policy engagements and outreach efforts.
  • Prepare regular updates for senior management and other audiences summarizing the initiative’s efforts and achievements toward financial sustainability of the region’s protected and conserved lands.
  • Lead analysis and research within the framework of the Pantanal and Gran Chaco strategy to gather scientific, policy, and technical information on protected area conservation lands finances and management in Latin America.
  • Represent Pew in external events online and in person, including meetings with national and local governments, multilateral organizations, and other institutions.
  • Participate in activities that support program and Pew-wide objectives.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree in public policy, economics, business, natural resources management or related studies preferred.
  • Generally, a minimum of 10 years
  • Fluency in both English and Spanish is required, competence in Portuguese is desired.
  • Significant experience in project management, financial mechanisms, and government engagement.
  • Experience working with local and regional governments.
  • Experience in the management of protected areas or other forms of conservation lands, including development of management plans, monitoring systems, and staff training programs.
  • Acute political awareness and understanding of issues from a non-partisan perspective.
  • Demonstrated experience building relationships across individuals and organizations with a range of interests and perspectives.
  • Capacity to lead group discussions with individuals working in different roles and countries; skilled in training and guiding team members with a high degree of cultural sensitivity.
  • Demonstrated experience meeting deadlines and effectively developing and moving projects forward with a high degree of independence and autonomy.
  • Effective professional writing skills in both English and Spanish. Effectively communicates ideas, thoughts and concepts clearly and concisely and in a compelling way, both written and orally.

Travel
Travel up to 25% of the time to cities and remote locations in Bolivia, Brazil, Argentina and throughout Latin America, and to the United States as necessary.


Work Authorization

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the country for which they are seeking employment without visa sponsorship.

Salary Range

The salary range represents a reasonable estimate of the annual salary based on Pew’s commitment to provide equitable and market-competitive pay. The actual salary offered will take into consideration many factors including but not limited to job-related knowledge, skills and experience, internal pay equity, and business need.

Total Rewards

This position offers a competitive salary and benefit program.

Pew is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, or any other protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Senior Project Engineer - Military Housing
jobs.excerpt: Ameresco, Inc.  (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions that provide reliable power and modernize infrastructure.
jobs.description:
Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC) is a leading energy infrastructure company delivering integrated solutions that provide reliable power and modernize infrastructure. Since 2000, we have served as a trusted partner to public and private sector customers across North America, the UK and Europe, delivering over $15 billion in solutions and contracting more than 5 GW of energy resources.

At Ameresco, we integrate energy resources and modernize the built environment through innovative infrastructure solutions that improve reliability, optimize performance, strengthen resilience, and support long-term sustainability. Join us in building the infrastructure that powers the future. Explore opportunities to make a meaningful impact while growing your career with a company at the forefront of energy innovation.


Ameresco currently has an opening for a Senior Project Engineer to join our Military Housing (MHPI) team to develop and implement energy efficiency, geothermal, solar PV, controls, and distributed energy projects across privatized military family housing portfolios. This is a remote U.S. position with occasional travel to installations and partner offices.


The Senior Project Engineer supports proposal, development, design, construction, commissioning, and operations of energy and infrastructure projects serving MHPI partners and military housing communities. The role bridges engineering, project management, and customer/partner coordination so projects meet guaranteed performance, schedule, budget, code, and resident-impact requirements.


Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate visits to military housing project sites to investigate and gather energy performance data for existing mechanical, electrical, HVAC, geothermal, plumbing, and control systems.
  • Perform utility and energy analysis, residential building load calculations, and preliminary engineering assessments to support project development and evaluation of potential solutions.
  • Identify opportunities for energy efficiency upgrades and distributed energy resources, including ground-source heat pumps (GSHP), water-source heat pumps (WSHP), solar PV, battery energy storage, building automation / EMS, lighting, envelope, and central plant improvements.
  • Develop preliminary and refined cost estimates covering engineering, equipment, construction, project management, commissioning, operations, and maintenance.
  • Support conceptual and detailed engineering design and coordinate with engineering/design subcontractors to develop complete, coordinated, and timely design documentation, including narrative scopes of work, drawings, specifications, and design-criteria packages.
  • Support evaluation of construction subcontractor bids and equipment vendor proposals to select best value based on performance, pricing, schedule, warranty, and compliance, including domestic content / ITC considerations where applicable.
  • Prepare written technical content for proposals, Investment Grade Audits (IGA), design narratives, progress reports, and customer/partner briefings.
  • Develop approaches for project commissioning (Cx) and measurement and verification (M&V) of energy savings in collaboration with Ameresco Cx, controls, and operations staff.
  • Ensure project scopes achieve guaranteed energy and performance metrics, meet partner and installation requirements, and comply with applicable industry standards, UFC/UFGS where relevant, codes, and MHPI contract obligations.
  • Provide engineering support through all project phases: proposal, development, design, construction, commissioning, and operations / O&M.
  • Work with the site or portfolio Project Manager on ongoing communication and coordination with MHPI partners (property managers / owners), installation stakeholders, utilities, and subcontractors, including status updates and remedies for delays or field issues.
  • Provide engineering support during construction to address field issues, support quality control, verify installation in accordance with design documents, and facilitate on-time, on-budget delivery in occupied housing environments.
  • Support controls, EMS, and MBCx platform integration for GSHP and other HVAC systems, including points lists, sequences, trending, alarming, and Yardi or other property-management interfaces where used.
  • Present reports defining project progress, problems, and recommended solutions to internal leadership and external partners.
  • Evaluate project results against energy, comfort, reliability, and financial targets and support project changes or interventions required to achieve contracted outputs.
  • Travel as required.
  • Perform other duties as required.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor of Science degree in an engineering discipline from a four-year accredited college or university.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • Minimum 5 years of prior experience in an engineering or project development role.
  • Ability to review confidential US security information.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience working on energy savings performance contracts (ESPC), utility energy service contracts (UESC), or similar guaranteed-savings / performance-contracting structures preferred.
  • Direct experience with military family housing, MHPI partners, or other large multifamily / privatized housing portfolios preferred.
  • Experience with geothermal wellfields, indoor hydronic loops, heat-pump selection, and multifamily load diversity (interior vs. end units) preferred.
  • Demonstrated understanding of engineering principles associated with energy efficiency and renewable energy technologies, including HVAC, building automation / EMS, building envelope, solar PV, battery energy storage, cogeneration/microgrids, power systems, and water/steam or hydronic distribution preferred.
  • Knowledge of measurement and verification (M&V) procedures (IPMVP or equivalent) preferred.
  • Experience using whole-building energy modeling and/or solar PV modeling software preferred.
  • Certification or progress toward Certified Energy Manager (CEM); CxA or similar commissioning credential preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including technical presentations to partners and internal leadership.
  • Valid driver’s license issued by state of residence and in good standing.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $107,100 - $155,100 (presented in good faith). In addition to base pay, employees receive a comprehensive benefits package, such as health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off, and may be eligible for performance incentives, bonuses, commissions, or equity, depending on the role.

Actual pay will depend on factors such as internal equity, skills, experience, education, certifications, and location. This range supports our commitment to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws. Compensation may vary by work location, including remote arrangements.

We disclose salary ranges and benefits in all required external and internal postings and will provide further details upon request at any stage of the hiring process. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Ameresco challenges the brightest, most talented, and creative individuals in the industry by providing an environment that fosters initiative and achievement. We are proud of our comprehensive and competitive employee benefits, including people-oriented insurance, investment, and incentive plans.

All official communications from Ameresco will originate from an @ameresco.com email address. Any correspondence from other domains should be regarded as fraudulent. Please report any suspicious activity to the platform where the issue was encountered. For further inquiries or concerns, please contact us at 1-866-AMERESCO

jobs.description:
Root was founded on the belief that car insurance is broken, and we set out to change it. We’re harnessing the power of technology to revolutionize this archaic, complicated industry. Using machine learning and mobile telematic platforms, we’ve built one of the most innovative insurtech companies in the world.

The Opportunity

The IT Audit Manager, Internal Audit and Internal Controls exists to lead the ongoing maintenance, evaluation, and testing of the organization’s IT general controls (ITGCs), application controls, and IT security controls for the SOX, Model Audit Rule (MAR), and Internal Audit programs. This role is expected to play a critical part in the continuing evolution of the internal technology control framework while managing audit projects across cloud infrastructure, engineering, data platforms, and core business systems as part of the Internal Audit function.

Success is achieved by providing strong project management over technology audits, reviewing technical workpapers for external and audit report readiness, leveraging AI to perform data analytics and visualization, and educating cross-functional business and engineering partners on maintaining a robust, scalable control environment. The ideal candidate combines hands-on IT audit expertise, strong supervisory skills, and a deep understanding of information security, modern technology architecture, and risk management.

Salary Range: $134,100 - $167,600(Eligible for competitive bonus and equity offering)

Root is a “work where it works best” company. Meaning we will support you working in whatever location that works best for you across the US. We will continue to have our headquarters in Columbus, Ohio.

How You Will Make an Impact

  • Lead IT Audit & Compliance Project Management: Drive project management efforts for the implementation, testing, and continuous monitoring of Root’s IT General Controls (ITGCs), automated application controls, SOC 1 reviews, and IT-dependent reporting to support SOX and Model Audit Rule (MAR) compliance.
  • Supervise & Guide Audit Execution: Lead and mentor IT auditors and cross-functional team members through complex technology processes, system implementations, and automated & manual controls.
  • Review Workpapers & External Audit Liaison: Review IT audit workpapers to ensure alignment with professional standards, audit readiness, and seamless coordination with external auditors and regulatory examiners.
  • Critical Technology Projects & System Launches: Partner proactively with engineering, product, and IT operations to ensure risk and control perspectives are assessed, designed, and implemented during critical business and technology initiatives.
  • Stakeholder Collaboration & Education: Work collaboratively with the Head of Internal Audit and Internal Controls and technology process owners (including engineering, InfoSec, and IT) to effectively communicate the value of proactive risk management and strong internal controls.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Data Architect – PBM Data Modernization

Location: Remote (US Only) Industry:Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM)Platform:Google Cloud Platform

Role Overview

We're looking for a Data Architect to lead data modeling and source-to-target mapping for a Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) modernization program on Google Cloud. The role covers migrating legacy claims and eligibility data, and the IBM Cognos reporting built on it, into a new BigQuery-based enterprise data warehouse. It also ensures the future-state platform meets state-specific Medicaid reporting requirements, starting with the MVP.

Key Responsibilities

  • Define the semantic and logical data models for MVP and future-state reporting, covering pharmacy claims, member eligibility, prescriber, pharmacy network, formulary, rebates, and pricing domains.
  • Own mapping execution end to end. Define source-to-target mappings, transformation rules, and business logic from legacy structures to the new warehouse.
  • Inventory and analyze legacy IBM Cognos (Cognos Explorer / Cognos Analytics) reports, packages, and Framework Manager models. Reverse-engineer embedded business logic and calculations, and rationalize reports for redesign on the future-state platform.
  • Set mapping standards, templates, naming conventions, and documentation practices. Direct the Data and Systems Analysts and review their work for quality and consistency.
  • Lead gap analysis and drive each gap to a decision (build, defer, workaround, or descope) with business, compliance, and technical stakeholders.
  • Translate state Medicaid reporting requirements (encounter data submissions, MCO/PBM transparency reports, spread pricing and pass-through disclosures, T-MSIS-aligned extracts) into data model and mapping specifications.
  • Define data quality rules, reconciliation checkpoints, and lineage so legacy-to-target results, including Cognos report outputs, are traceable and audit-ready.
Work with data engineers on ingestion and transformation design on GCP, and use Vertex AI and Gemini to speed up mapping, profiling, and documentation.

Requirements

Qualifications

  • 10+ years in data architecture or data modeling, with at least 3 years in PBM, pharmacy, or health plan data.
  • Hands-on experience with NCPDP claim standards, Medicaid and managed care reporting, and legacy migration programs.
  • Strong skills in dimensional and semantic modeling, plus advanced SQL.
  • Experience with IBM Cognos Analytics / Cognos Explorer, including Framework Manager packages, report specifications, and migrating Cognos reporting to a modern BI platform.
  • Hands-on experience with Google Cloud data services:
  • BigQuery for warehouse design, including partitioning, clustering, and authorized views
  • Dataflow and Dataproc for transformation pipelines
  • Cloud Composer (Airflow) for orchestration

–Cloud Storage for landing zones

  • Dataform or dbt for SQL-based transformations
  • Familiarity with Dataplex and Data Catalog for metadata, lineage, and data quality, and with Looker (LookML) for building the semantic layer.
  • Proven experience leading analyst teams and running mapping governance.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA, CMS regulations, and state-level Medicaid compliance, along with GCP security controls (IAM, VPC Service Controls, CMEK).
  • Location & Work Authorization: Must currently reside in the United States and hold valid US work authorization without sponsorship.

Nice to Have

  • Exposure to Vertex AI or Gemini in BigQuery for AI-assisted mapping, profiling, and documentation.
  • Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer or Professional Cloud Architect certification.

jobs.excerpt: About the roleEvery project needs the right linguists at the right time, and you'll make sure it has them.
jobs.description:
About the role

Every project needs the right linguists at the right time, and you'll make sure it has them. As Resource Coordinator, you'll find the right linguists for projects on our platform, assign their tasks, and follow up so work is delivered on time, within budget, and at the quality our customers expect. You'll report to our Production Manager, be the day-to-day contact for our linguists, and help keep our linguist pools up to date and our community happy. You'll do well here if you're organized, stay calm when priorities change, and like to keep developing your skills.

What you'll do

  • Find the right linguists for running tasks on our platform, assign post-editors, revisers, and other linguists to specific tasks, and follow up on their progress.
  • Decide on and set priorities for ongoing tasks, so projects meet their deadlines, stay within cost, and meet quality expectations.
  • Communicate with linguists and make sure they have everything they need to work on their tasks.
  • Work with the Production Manager to make sure quality expectations are met, linguist pools have enough people to meet deadlines, and all pools stay up to date, and give them daily feedback.
  • Monitor how satisfied our linguist community is.

What you'll bring

  • typically 2+ years of progressive experience in resourcing, project management, or linguistic work, or equivalent experience
  • higher education, ideally at postgraduate level
  • excellent written and spoken English, and good knowledge of Microsoft Office
  • strong organization and attention to detail, delivering reports, replies, and results on time, adapting when circumstances change, and staying in control under pressure
  • good analytical and communication skills, including quickly understanding the core of a complex problem and the details that lead to a solution

Nice to have

  • a degree in languages or linguistics
  • advanced Microsoft Excel skills
  • a second foreign language

If you have some of these, great. If you don't, we'd still like to hear from you.

Who we are

At Acclaro, we're more than a localization company — we're a content intelligence solutions company, and a global team of language enthusiasts, cultural connectors, and technology innovators. Our mission is to help brands speak the world's languages and resonate deeply across cultures by blending human expertise with cutting-edge technology, delivered through a follow-the-sun model that keeps our teams moving around the clock and around the globe.

With over two decades of experience, we support some of the world's most recognizable brands in expanding their global reach. And we're scaling: we've been making material investments in our own AI-native platform, one that's already reshaping how our business — and the localization industry more broadly — works. Join us on our journey to be the model localization company of the next decade, one that's loved by clients, colleagues, and communities alike.

How we work

Our values shape how we work with customers, colleagues, and partners. Here's what you can expect from us, and what we'll look for in you.

  • Be Accountable. We own our work, learn from our mistakes, and come with solutions.
  • Be Proud. We care about the work, hold a high standard, and celebrate each other's wins.
  • Be Resilient. When things get hard, we stay calm, adapt, and ask for help when we need it.
  • Be Curious. We ask why, keep learning, share what we know, and explore new ways of working, including AI.
  • Be Kind. We assume good intent, give honest feedback with care, and look out for each other.

Pay

Pay range: $21,000,000 - $23,000,000 gross per year base salary, depending on experience.

Inclusion and equal opportunity

Acclaro is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

We assess every candidate against the same criteria. If you need a reasonable accommodation to take part in any stage of our hiring process, let your recruiter know. We'll work with you to find a solution and keep what you share confidential.

jobs.title: Sr. Clinical Data Manager
jobs.excerpt: Alimentiv is a global CRO with a singular focus: advancing therapies for patients with gastrointestinal diseases.
jobs.description:
Alimentiv is a global CRO with a singular focus: advancing therapies for patients with gastrointestinal diseases. GI is our WHY and for more than 30 years that purpose has driven our scientific rigour, operational excellence, and deep therapeutic expertise, including supporting more than 70% of IBD compounds in development.
We operate as a private, profit-with-purpose company, channeling our commercial success back into scientific research, technology, and our people. With approximately 700 people across multiple countries and three service lines, we are growing deliberately, and the capability of our leaders and our organization is central to how we get there.

If you want to do meaningful work, build something real, and invest back in research that changes lives — we want to meet you!

Job Overview

Responsible for leading, planning and execution of all data management activities for assigned projects, ensuring focus on data integrity, validity, reliability in accordance with standard processes, sponsor guidelines, industry best practices and regulatory standards. Act as coach, mentor and/or Subject Matter Expert within the department, aiding Manager in process improvements, issue escalation and training development and delivery. Support the department and company in achieving objectives and strategic goals.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead Data Management Operations Serve as primary contact overseeing all data management activities from study start-up through database lock, including data management plan creation, CRF development, database specifications, edit check testing, and data review processes.
  • Database Development & Quality Control Coordinate database build and testing with programmers, define and validate edit checks, perform data review and query management, and process/reconcile electronic data from multiple sources (CIMS, Safety database, labs, IRT).
  • Team Leadership & Supervision Coordinate and supervise 1-7 Data Management staff members, providing training, mentorship, and conducting performance reviews while managing project resources within budget and timelines.
  • Stakeholder Communication & Project Coordination Participate in and lead internal/sponsor meetings, work directly with project managers and teams, track study progress, issue status reports, and serve as escalation point for data-related issues.
  • Training & Documentation Management Develop and deliver training programs for investigators, clinical sites, project teams and sponsors on data collection processes and tools; ensure study documentation is maintained and properly stored in trial master files.
  • Department Development & Process Improvement Contribute to continuous improvement through information sharing, coach and mentor peers, participate in or lead development of SOPs/policies, and support cross-functional working groups.
  • Strategic Support & Advocacy Act as Subject Matter Expert within the department, support manager with process improvements and issue escalation, and promote data management excellence internally and externally.
  • Compliance & Standards Ensure all activities adhere to standard processes, sponsor guidelines, industry best practices, and regulatory standards while supporting departmental and company strategic goals.

Skills & Qualifications

  • A minimum of a one-to-two-year post-secondary certification in a relevant field of study, and 4-6 years of related work experience in Clinical Data Management with ongoing training.
  • Life Sciences or Clinical Research specialty and CCDM (Certified Clinical Data Manager) certification preferred.
  • Ability to set personal pace and prioritize tasks with significant autonomy.
  • Strong interpersonal skills with patience and tact for managing regular contacts with team members, vendors, and clients

What We Offer

    In addition, as an Alimentiv Employee, you’re also eligible for the following programs:

    • Education Reimbursement program for full-time employees
    • Monthly Cell Phone and Remote Work Allowance (dependent on role eligibility)
    • One time office setup allowance (can be used to purchase a scanner/printer, extra monitor, office furniture, etc.)
    • Working while visiting program – up to 4 weeks per year!
    • Flexible Summer Hours Program from May – September
    • Employee referral incentive – we know great people know other great people, and we think that warrants recognition!
    • Full-time employees also become beneficiaries of the Alimentiv Trust after one year of employment, and permanent members after 5 years of employment
    • Optional formal mentorship program (Alimentorship); country/region annual social events in person; leadership development programs for people leaders in accordance with your seniority; social committee and several other optional initiatives designed to support you in feeling like part of the Alimentiv team!

      • Additional benefits may be available depending on the country of employment and are subject to local policies and eligibility.

Our Services

  • End-to-end GI clinical trial services, from protocol design through submission support
  • Central medical imaging management and endoscopic reading
  • Precision medicine and biomarker solutions
  • Real-world evidence and clinical consulting
  • Histopathology and lab services through AcelaBio

How to Apply

    To apply for this position, please submit your resume through the Alimentiv Careers Portal or via LinkedIn’s Easy Apply. Resumes must be submitted in English.

Equal Opportunity and Accessibility

    Alimentiv is committed to building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, ethnicity, national origin, religion or belief, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital or family status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
    Accommodations are available upon request for persons with disabilities throughout the recruitment and selection process. Requests can be directed to .
Stay Alert to Recruitment Scams

Alimentiv is aware of a continued increase in phishing scams, which use various methods of attack via email, text, voice and social media, including individuals posing as our recruiters and contacting candidates with fraudulent opportunities. Our hiring process always includes direct engagement with a recruiter or hiring manager, and we will never ask for sensitive personal information early in the process.

Official communication will only come from company email addresses containing "@alimentiv.com". If you are contacted about an open job at Alimentiv, please verify the domain of the sender's email address and confirm that you are being asked to apply on this website. If something doesn't feel right, we encourage you to verify before responding. If you believe you have been the victim of a phishing scam, please contact your local government cyber authority to report it.

Job Title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics & Embodied AI Research

Job Type: Full-time

Location: Remote

The Role

We're hiring a Robotics Researcher to drive frontier research in embodied AI, robot learning, and physical AI systems.

This is a hands-on research role focused on advancing vision-language-action (VLA) models, generalist robot policies, world models, and emerging approaches to embodied intelligence. You'll design and execute end-to-end robotics experiments, leveraging real-world data, simulation, and human-in-the-loop systems to evaluate and improve robot performance.

You'll independently explore promising research directions and collaborate with leading AI and robotics teams to translate experimental findings into scalable solutions.

What You'll Do

  1. Lead frontier robotics research across VLA models, generalist policies, world models, and emerging embodied AI approaches.
  2. Design end-to-end experimentation systems spanning teleoperation, data collection, simulation, policy deployment, and real-world evaluation.
  3. Develop high-fidelity simulations using real-world data to evaluate robot policies and validate performance in physical environments.
  4. Leverage flow, our human-in-the-loop annotation platform, to structure and scale robotics datasets from egocentric video, teleoperation demonstrations, and multimodal sensor data.
  5. Investigate model limitations, failure modes, and sim-to-real gaps to develop improved datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies.
  6. Rapidly prototype and validate novel approaches to robot learning, policy optimization, and embodied intelligence.
  7. Independently identify high-impact research opportunities and lead projects from initial exploration through experimentation and scalable implementation.

What We're Looking For

  1. Strong background in robotics, embodied AI, robot learning, computer vision, or applied machine learning research.
  2. Hands-on experience developing, training, or evaluating robot learning models, including VLA models, imitation learning, or generalist policies.
  3. Proficiency in Python and experience with robotics or ML frameworks such as PyTorch, ROS, or simulation environments.
  4. Experience designing robotics experiments involving real-world data collection, simulation, policy evaluation, or hardware deployment.
  5. Understanding of robot learning methodologies, multimodal perception, and sim-to-real transfer challenges.
  6. Ability to analyze model behavior, identify failure modes, and translate research findings into measurable performance improvements.
  7. Strong research ownership, experimental judgment, and ability to independently execute complex technical projects.
  8. Strong technical communication and collaboration skills across research and engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience with world models, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or diffusion-based robot policies.
  2. Hands-on experience with teleoperation, robotics hardware, sensor integration, or real-world policy deployment.
  3. Familiarity with robotics simulators such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or comparable environments.
  4. Experience building multimodal robotics datasets from egocentric video, robot trajectories, or sensor data.
  5. Prior experience at a leading robotics or frontier AI research lab.

Responsibilities

Peraton is hiring an experienced Open Science Professional/Scientist to support the CDC OSQLS Knowledge Management (KM) Team in advancing Open Science, public access, research transparency, and reproducibility across the agency. The CDC OSQLS KM Team supports systems and services for electronic scientific clearance, public access, content management, document routing, research compliance, and scientific publishing across CDC Centers, Institutes, and Offices (CIOs). The team also supports the CDC Stacks public repository and internal systems that facilitate scientific research and publishing.

As CDC expands its Open Science practices, the selected candidate will help researchers develop transparent and reproducible research packages, improve KM systems and workflows, and develop training and guidance to support Open Science implementation across CDC.

Key Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Develop and co-author Open Science training materials, guidelines, and implementation resources.
  • Propose enhancements to KM systems and tools that strengthen Open Science practices.
  • Develop and recommend Open Science workflows supporting research transparency, reproducibility, and compliance.
  • Work directly with CDC researchers to integrate Open Science principles into research workflows.
  • Liaise with CDC Centers, Institutes, and Offices (CIOs) to provide Open Science outreach, instruction, and research support.
  • Provide reference and research support to researchers seeking guidance on Open Science implementation.
  • Collaborate with CDC scientific leadership and CIO staff to implement Open Science practices.
  • Participate, as appropriate, in CDC and federal Open Science committees and working groups.
  • Adapt activities and deliverables as CDC Open Science policies, practices, and implementation priorities evolve.

Qualifications

Basic Requirements:

  • 5 years with BS/BA; 3 years with MS/MA; 0 years with PhD
  • Knowledge of Open Science policies, guidelines, and practices, including U.S. Public Access policies, the Gold Standard Science memorandum, and Open Data policy and law.
  • Experience with Open Science tools such as DMPTool, Open Science Framework (OSF), GitHub, repository platforms, and data documentation tools.

If you're familiar with Salesforce JumpStarts you know that this work is limited engagement implementations focused on getting clients up and running quickly using out-of-the-box configuration, best practices, and standard functionality. No heavy customization, no complex development. Discovery, configuration, data import, user setup, and training. Clean, repeatable, time-boxed projects. Lumicera Health Services is seeking a Wholesaler Relations & Contracting Manager to join our team!

The Wholesaler Relations & Contracting Manager remains actively engaged after implementation to support contract performance, resolve issues, and strengthen long-term partner relationships. This highly collaborative, external-facing role requires an understanding of pharmaceutical distribution and the ability to work across relationship management, business development, contracting, and execution. The Manager works closely with Clarventa leadership and cross-functional teams to advance opportunities from initial discussion through contracting, implementation, and ongoing performance management.

Is this you? Find out more below!

  • Develop partner strategies and action plans that expand participation, purchasing volume, contract utilization, and long-term engagement across the Clarventa network.
  • Convert partnership opportunities into signed, executable agreements and coordinate with internal stakeholders through contracting, implementation, and launch.
  • Understand wholesaler business needs and effectively position Clarventa’s network, aggregated demand, reporting capabilities, and partnership model to external stakeholders.
  • Monitor purchasing activity, participation trends, reporting, and partner performance to identify growth opportunities, risks, and areas requiring action.
  • Partner with analytics and operations teams to provide performance visibility and actionable insights that support partner decision-making and network growth.
  • Facilitate communication among wholesalers, member pharmacies, manufacturers, and internal stakeholders to resolve contracting, eligibility, reporting, operational, and relationship issues.
  • Support contract awareness, network engagement, and ongoing relationship management after implementation to help agreements become active, productive partnerships.
  • Build and maintain a pipeline of wholesaler opportunities, renewals, expansions, and strategic initiatives, with clear ownership of next steps and outcomes.

  • Other duties as assigned.

  • 5+ years of experience in pharmaceutical distribution, specialty pharmacy, pharmacy GPOs, or related healthcare commercial roles required.

jobs.description:
Job Summary:

The Regional Accountant makes sure every entity in the region reports complete, accurate and compliant results before they roll up to the portfolio.

The role is the portfolio's finance link to the region's Business Units (BU). It reviews close deliverables, investigates variances, reconciles intercompany balances, and oversees local tax obligations. It gives the Portfolio Reporting Consolidation Manager a single, reliable point of contact and early warning of issues for each region.

Job Description:

Key responsibilities


1. Regional point of contact

  • Act as the primary point of contact between the Portfolio Reporting Consolidation Manager and the BUs in the region.
  • Communicate portfolio reporting timetables, templates and requirements to BU finance teams, and follow up on outstanding deliverables.
  • Build working relationships with BU finance staff so issues surface early.

2. Period-end review

  • Review month-end, quarter-end and year-end results and close deliverables for entities in the region.
  • Confirm completeness, accuracy and consistency with portfolio policies before results roll up to the portfolio.
  • Track open review points with BUs through to resolution within the close timetable.

3. Variance and balance analysis

  • Investigate unusual entity-level variances and balances to confirm the accuracy of reported results.
  • Obtain explanations and supporting evidence from BUs where movements are not self-evident.
  • Flag issues, potential misstatements and judgement areas to the Portfolio Reporting Consolidation Manager and Sub-Portfolio Finance Lead.

4. Tax compliance

  • Review and support BUs to ensure tax compliance for entities in the region, including indirect taxes (GST, VAT, US sales tax) and income tax returns.
  • Support BUs working with external tax advisors on preparation, review and lodgment of returns, and respond to their information requests.
  • Maintain a regional tax compliance calendar so filing deadlines are met.

5. Intercompany reconciliation

  • Ensure intercompany balances reconcile for entities in the region each period.
  • Investigate and resolve mismatches with counterparty entities, including those in other regions.
  • Escalate unresolved differences before consolidation deadlines.

6. Regulatory awareness

  • Maintain knowledge of local accounting, tax and regulatory requirements in the region.
  • Flag changes to the Portfolio Reporting Consolidation Manager and the Director of GRC, with an initial view of the impact.

7. Reconciliation review (OneStream)

  • Review OneStream reconciliations to confirm work papers and supporting documentation match the balance sheet.
  • Report any concerns or discrepancies to the Portfolio Reporting Consolidation Manager, copying the relevant Sub-Portfolio Finance Leads.

8. Other

  • Support portfolio projects such as system implementations, acquisition onboarding and process improvement, as directed.
  • Perform other duties consistent with the role, as reasonably required.

Worker Type:

Regular

Number of Openings Available:

1

  • Proven industry experience through multiple major product releases in a commercial SaaS environment.

  • Solid understanding of transformer models and LLM-based approaches, including hands-on experience with prompt tuning and PEFT methods (e.g. LoRA, QLoRA) using frameworks such as Hugging Face Transformers.
  • Experience building and evaluating models using modern ML packages such as NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, PyTorch, and LightGBM.
  • Experience building and deploying models using public cloud infrastructure (Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud), including familiarity with version control, CI/CD pipelines, and scaling considerations for production ML systems at SaaS scale.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills; comfortable working on a distributed team.
  • Experience with one or more of: reinforcement learning or RLHF, NLP techniques for summarization, extraction, classification, or semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines and/or agentic frameworks (e.g. LangChain, LlamaIndex).

The Media Sales Specialist is responsible for converting broadcasters, publishers, and streaming platforms into paying clients — and expanding those relationships into meaningful, recurring revenue.

Partnership Growth

  • Track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals (preferably multi-year partnerships)

The role brings together distribution performance, lead analytics, market opportunity, and external trends to identify where Horace Mann should recruit, expand, invest, or adjust coverage. The leader will turn complex data into practical recommendations, build decision-support capabilities, and partner across the enterprise to move insight into sustained execution.

This role leads and develops a team of approximately four strategy and analytics professionals, with the capacity to scale as business needs evolve.

  • Lead Marketing and Distribution strategy, analytics, and planning across Local Agent, Call Center, Partnerships, and Internet channels.

  • Build and operationalize dashboards, self-service tools, scorecards, and decision-support capabilities that make performance transparent and actionable.
  • Deliver proactive insights, scenarios, and executive narratives that clearly communicate opportunities, risks, and tradeoffs.
  • Monitor consumer, competitor, economic, technology, and distribution trends and assess their implications for strategy, demand, channel mix, and growth.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives with Marketing, Distribution, Finance, Operations, Data and Technology, and other partners from problem definition through implementation and operating adoption.
  • Establish analytics standards, metric definitions, data-quality expectations, and disciplined performance routines across channels.

Qualifications

Full-time employee - Remote

The Salesforce Technical Lead will ensure the successful implementation of system updates, provide operational support, optimize system performance, and manage the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) to maintain high-quality and efficient service delivery. Additionally, the Salesforce Technical Lead will maintain integrations between Salesforce Orgs and external systems, ensuring seamless data flow, and conduct knowledge transfer activities to equip client staff with the necessary skills and expertise for continued operational success. The Salesforce Technical Lead will also be responsible for the procurement and management of Salesforce licenses for the supported orgs, ensuring alignment with system requirements and user needs.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, AI Implementations
jobs.excerpt: BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals.
jobs.description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

​General Description:

The Global Commercial and Medical Affairs Technology team at BeOne is seeking a Senior Manager, AI implementation to help operationalize AI capabilities across Commercial and Medical teams. This role sits at the intersection of oncology data, customer and patient journey data, GenAI implementation, and enterprise data platforms.

This role will help define the semantic layer over BeOne's commercial and medical data warehouse, ensuring structured and unstructured data assets are described consistently so AI models, RAG experiences, insight engines, and BI layers can leverage the right data with the right context.

The Senior Manager will coordinate with Commercial, Medical, Data Engineering, Data Science, Compliance, Privacy, and field teams to ensure free-text insight collection, RAG chat interfaces, AI-generated outputs, and customer journey solutions are implemented with appropriate guardrails, traceability, and business relevance.

The ideal candidate brings 3-5 years of recent oncology experience focused on patient journeys and patient-level data, strong familiarity with commercial and medical data ecosystems, and a hands-on builder mindset with the ability to write code, explore emerging platforms, and turn AI concepts into practical capabilities that make cross-functional workstreams more efficient.

Key Responsibilities:

Semantic Layer, Data Context & Insight Engine

  • Lead creation and ongoing governance of a semantic layer on top of the commercial and medical data warehouse, including entities, attributes, definitions, metrics, business rules, relationships, lineage, and data quality expectations.
  • Partner with data engineering, BI, MDM, and business stakeholders to define how patient, HCP, account, field insight, engagement, journey, patient-level, and medical/commercial data assets should be represented for AI use.
  • Translate data definitions and business context into reusable metadata, ontologies, knowledge objects, and retrieval patterns that improve AI model grounding.
  • Support the design of an insight generation engine on top of the data and semantic layers, ensuring outputs are accurate, explainable, timely, and available through the appropriate BI and workflow layers.
  • Define evaluation criteria for data readiness, retrieval quality, insight accuracy, confidence, freshness, source attribution, and business actionability.

Commercial & Medical AI Guardrails

  • Coordinate across Commercial, Medical, field, compliance, privacy, legal, and technology teams to ensure AI guardrails for free-text inputs and field-collected insights are implemented correctly.
  • Establish practical operating procedures for acceptable use, input validation, sensitive data handling, prompt and response controls, human review, and exception management.
  • Monitor adoption and quality of field insight capture workflows, identifying risks related to incomplete context, inconsistent terminology, duplication, bias, hallucination, or inappropriate data use.
  • Ensure AI outputs appropriately reflect approved data sources, business rules, medical/legal/regulatory considerations, and commercial/medical operating boundaries.

RAG, Chat & Knowledge Retrieval Solutions

  • Validate and continuously improve RAG-based chat interfaces across Commercial and Medical teams, including source coverage, retrieval performance, answer quality, citation/traceability, feedback loops, and escalation paths.
  • Work with teams to ensure data and unstructured knowledge assets are collected, curated, permissions-aware, and available for use in chat, summarization, insight, and assistant experiences.
  • Partner with data science and engineering teams to refine embeddings, chunking strategies, metadata filters, prompt templates, evaluation datasets, and LLMOps/monitoring capabilities.
  • Design and run testing processes to confirm RAG outputs are accurate, grounded, consistent, and fit for use in business and medical workflows.

AI-Generated Meeting-Ready Outputs

  • Enhance existing RAG and GenAI models to generate meeting-ready decks, briefs, summaries, talking points, and insight narratives based on unstructured commercial and medical content.
  • Define reusable templates and quality checks for AI-generated presentation materials, including audience, purpose, key message, evidence, caveats, next-best-action, and source attribution.
  • Partner with field, brand, medical, and other commercial teams to connect unstructured content with structured data and BI outputs so meeting materials are timely and decision ready.
  • Drive adoption of automation that reduces manual preparation time while maintaining quality, compliance, and stakeholder trust.

End-to-End Customer Journey & BI Integration

  • Ensure end-to-end customer and patient journey solutions leverage AI capabilities in the intended manner, grounded in BeOne's data landscape and aligned to priority use cases.
  • Map AI use cases to upstream data sources, semantic definitions, model workflows, BI outputs, CRM/field workflows, and user actions.
  • Partner with Commercial and Medical teams to validate that AI-generated insights are reflected accurately and timely in dashboards, reporting layers, and performance-management routines.
  • Bring oncology patient journey expertise to ensure AI-driven insights are clinically and commercially meaningful, with appropriate granularity and limitations clearly understood.

Hands-on Prototyping & Enterprise Implementation

  • Write code and build prototypes, scripts, prompts, evaluation harnesses, APIs, or workflow automations to test and accelerate new AI capabilities.
  • Explore emerging AI platforms, data products, and vendor capabilities; recommend practical fit-for-purpose solutions and help transition successful experiments into scalable delivery.
  • Engage with Corporate Affairs, Procurement, Clinical, and other enterprise teams to identify and support AI solutions that improve efficiency in high-value tasks.
  • Produce documentation, training, demos, and user guidance that help teams adopt AI responsibly and effectively.
  • Support roadmap planning, backlog prioritization, vendor coordination, delivery milestones, and measurement of value/impact.

Governance, Security & Compliance

  • Apply AI governance, model validation/evaluation, data privacy, information security, and regulatory expectations, including HIPAA, GDPR, GxP where applicable.
  • Document model assumptions, source data, prompts, retrieval configurations, known limitations, review controls, and audit trails.
  • Partner with compliance, legal, privacy, and security teams to ensure patient-level data handling, role-based access controls, and promotional/medical content boundaries are respected.
  • Implement monitoring and feedback mechanisms for accuracy, data quality, fairness, hallucination risk, user experience, and operational performance.

Education Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in AI, Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Biomedical Informatics, Life Sciences, or a related quantitative/technical field; Master's degree preferred.

Qualifications:

Technical & Domain Expertise

  • BS Degree with 7+ years of experience across data products, AI/ML, GenAI implementation, data engineering, BI, or commercial/medical technology in enterprise environments.
  • 3+ years of recent oncology experience focused on patient journeys, patient-level data, customer/HCP engagement, commercial domain, medical domain, and related domain knowledge.
  • Strong understanding of pharmaceutical/biotech commercial and medical data ecosystems, including patient journey data, field insights, CRM/field activity, medical/commercial knowledge assets, omnichannel engagement, and BI/reporting layers.
  • Experience building or governing semantic layers, data catalogs, business glossaries, metadata frameworks, ontologies, knowledge graphs, or metrics layers for AI use.
  • Hands-on experience with GenAI/RAG concepts, including document ingestion, embeddings, vector databases, retrieval strategies, prompt engineering, grounding, evaluation, monitoring, and guardrails.
  • Coding proficiency in Python and SQL; ability to prototype independently and partner effectively with engineering teams.
  • Experience with data warehouse, lakehouse, and cloud platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Azure, or GCP; experience with BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, or similar preferred.
  • Familiarity with LLMOps/MLOps, APIs, workflow automation, data pipelines, and unstructured data processing.
  • Understanding of data privacy, security, compliance, and responsible AI practices in healthcare/life sciences environments.

Business Acumen & Leadership

  • Ability to translate ambiguous business needs into practical AI/data products and technical requirements.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration with Commercial, Medical, field teams, data science, engineering, BI, compliance, privacy, legal, procurement, corporate affairs, clinical, and vendor partners.
  • Executive-ready communication and storytelling skills; ability to explain AI outputs, data limitations, and recommended actions to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive adoption, standardization, and change management across matrixed teams.
  • Builder mindset; comfortable testing new tools, writing code, learning quickly, and moving from proof-of-concept to scalable capability.
  • Strong project/product management skills, including prioritization, requirements definition, delivery coordination, and value measurement.

Nice to Have

  • Advanced degree in AI, data science, biomedical informatics, life sciences, computer science, statistics, engineering, or related field.
  • Experience with oncology product launch, patient-level claims/EHR/EMR data, data tokenization/identity resolution, MDM, or customer 360 capabilities.
  • Experience with automated deck generation, document intelligence, copilot/assistant experiences, or agentic workflows.

Travel

locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Remote Clinical Trial Support Specialist
(Multiple Openings)
Company: Angel City VA — Virtual Clinical Research Support.
Location: Remote (Philippines, Latin America,Georgia, Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia, Azerbajan) .
Employment Type: Full-Time, Part-Time, and Project-Based Opportunities Available
Join Angel City VA — Where Top Clinical Research Talent Gets Discovered.
Angel City VA is a Los Angeles-based, fast-scaling virtual support platform built to power the next generation of clinical research. We partner with independent research sites, sponsors, and CROs to deliver the high-quality remote clinical trial support that keeps studies moving, and demand for our services is growing fast. Our team thrives in a high-energy, fast-paced, and genuinely collaborative environment where sharp, driven professionals do work that matters: advancing the trials that bring new treatments to patients who need it the most. This is your chance to grow alongside a company that is expanding rapidly across the world and investing in the people who make it run.
Here’s the key thing to know: we are actively building a database of high-caliber, pre-qualified candidates from which we draw to staff independent research sites as new opportunities come online. Applying now puts you on our radar early. When the right study or site need arises, we reach out first to the standout talent already in our global pipeline. If you’re ambitious, detail-obsessed, passionate about cutting-edge, scientifically-rigorous, and ethical patient care and ready to be part of something scaling fast, we want to meet you.
About the Role.
We are seeking experienced remote professionals (2-3 years of experience, medical/biopharmaceutical background, and with completed and current GCP and HIPAA training) to support independent clinical research sites, sponsors, Contract Research Organizations (CROs), and healthcare organizations across a wide range of clinical trial operations functions.
This is a multi-disciplinary opportunity designed to identify candidates with expertise in one or more areas of clinical research, patient engagement, regulatory support, study operations, finance, administration, and sponsor relations. Candidates are not expected to have experience in every area listed below.
Applicants should clearly indicate in their resume and cover letter which functional areas best match their experience and qualifications. Successful candidates will submit 3 references from previous clinical trial positions and will facilitate background checks as needed.
Potential Areas of Responsibility.
Angel City VA supports the full clinical trial lifecycle. The functional areas below reflect the services we provide to our research-site partners. Tell us where your strengths are. We can’t wait to learn about you.
Patient Education & Engagement
• Walk participants through study procedures and visit expectations at each stage of the trial.
• Support the informed-consent process and patient education initiatives.
• Deliver retention touchpoints and follow-up across the full study timeline.
• Answer participant questions and facilitate communication between patients and study teams.
Visit Scheduling & Coordination
• Book participant visits within protocol-defined windows.
• Send appointment reminders and confirmations.
• Conduct proactive follow-up to reduce no-shows and missed visits.
• Track attendance, book transportation, and resolve scheduling conflicts.
• Assist with scheduled patient visits by walking on-site medical staff through protocol-required procedures and documenting visits in electronic source and other systems as needed.
Patient Recruitment & Pre-Screening
• Conduct outreach to prospective study participants.
• Review charts, databases, and referral sources.
• Perform preliminary eligibility screening against study inclusion/exclusion criteria.
• Consult with principal and sub-investigators on suitability of patients for a trial.
• Schedule screening appointments and document recruitment activity.
• Minimize screen failure and maximize patient enrollment and retention.
Study Lead Generation
• Source sponsor and CRO study opportunities.
• Support feasibility-questionnaire responses.
• Track the pipeline for new study awards.
• Research upcoming trials and potential new business.
EHR / EMR Management
• Update and maintain electronic medical records accurately.
• Provide documentation support and chart-completion assistance.
• Support record organization and documentation workflows.
• Maintain compliance with applicable privacy and regulatory requirements.
Data Entry & Source Management
• Enter and maintain data in CTMS, EDC, and other research systems.
• Support query identification and resolution.
• Organize and maintain source documentation.
• Help ensure data is timely, accurate, and audit-ready.
Regulatory Support
• Maintain e-regulatory binders and essential staff documents.
• Manage document version control.
• Track expiration of licenses, certifications, training records, and delegation logs.
• Assist with submissions to sponsors, CROs, IRBs/ECs, and regulatory agencies.
Quality Assurance Support
• Prepare for source-data verification (SDV).
• Log protocol deviations and support corrective/preventive actions.
• Support audit and monitoring-visit readiness.
• Help maintain inspection-ready documentation.
Patient & IP Compliance Support
• Deliver dosing and adherence reminders.
• Follow up on e-diary compliance.
• Maintain investigational product (IP) accountability logs.
• Support participant compliance throughout the treatment period.
Contract & Budget Negotiation Support
• Support clinical trial agreement (CTA) and budget drafting/negotiations.
• Track redlines and contract revisions.
• Reconcile payment terms and financial milestones.
• Maintain organized contract and budget records.
Sponsor / CRO Relations Management
• Serve as a liaison across sponsors, CROs, and study stakeholders.
• Schedule meetings and track action items.
• Monitor deliverables and timelines.
• Support ongoing relationship coordination and stakeholder engagement.
Reimbursement & Stipend Coordination
• Process participant travel reimbursements and stipends.
• Support insurance verification and prior-authorization activities.
• Maintain accurate payment and reimbursement records.
Bookkeeping & Accounting
• Record financial transactions.
• Track accounts payable and accounts receivable.
• Perform reconciliation activities.
• Support financial documentation and record-keeping.
Finance Support
• Prepare and process invoices.
• Track payments and outstanding balances.
• Assist with financial reporting and analysis.
Bilingual Participant Support
• Communicate with participants in multiple languages across a diverse patient population.
• Provide culturally sensitive, patient-facing support.
• Assist with translation and localization of non-medical study communications as needed.
Administrative & Credentialing Support
• Collect and organize onboarding documentation.
• Track staff credentials, certifications, and required training.
• Maintain personnel files and compliance records.
• Support administrative projects and operational initiatives.
IP Remote Temperature Monitoring & Documentation
• Monitor investigational product storage temperatures remotely.
• Document temperature logs and identify excursions.
• Escalate temperature excursions per protocol and sponsor requirements.
• Maintain accurate, inspection-ready temperature records.
Site Monitoring Support (Pre-SIV, Pre-Interim, Pre-COV & Audit Preparation)
• Prepare sites and documentation ahead of Site Initiation Visits (SIVs).
• Support readiness for interim and routine monitoring visits.
• Prepare documentation and logistics for Close-Out Visits (COVs).
• Coordinate audit and inspection-preparation activities.
Clinical Trial Operations & Study Startup Support
• Assist with study startup, maintenance, and closeout activities.
• Support investigator meetings and site activation.
• Maintain operational records, trackers, and study milestones.
• Track action items across the study team.
Adverse Event & Safety Reporting Support
• Support timely logging of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs).
• Assist with safety-document distribution and acknowledgment tracking.
• Help maintain safety-reporting timelines and documentation.
Telehealth & Decentralized Trial (DCT) Support
• Coordinate and support virtual and telehealth study visits.
• Assist participants with study apps, devices, and eConsent platforms.
• Support remote data capture and decentralized-trial workflows.
Qualifications.
Candidates may qualify through experience in one or more of the following areas:
• Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) / Clinical Research Assistant or CRA support
• Study Startup Specialist / Regulatory Coordinator / Data Coordinator
• Patient Recruitment Specialist
• Clinical Trial Business Development / Sponsor or CRO Relations
• Healthcare Administration / Medical Office Management
• Finance, Accounting, or Bookkeeping support
• Credentialing Specialist / Remote Healthcare Operations / EHR/EMR Management
• Clinical Trial Quality Assurance
• Pharmacovigilance or Safety Reporting support
• Telehealth / Decentralized Clinical Trial (DCT) coordination
Preferred Qualifications
• 2-3 years of experience supporting clinical trials, research sites, CROs, sponsors, or healthcare organizations.
• Medical or biopharmaceutical background, education, or equivalent experience (e.g., life sciences degree, nursing/allied health, pharmacy, or prior clinical research experience).
• Completed and current GCP and HIPAA training
• Familiarity with GCP (Good Clinical Practice) principles and ICH E6(R3) guidelines.
• Experience with CTMS, EDC, EMR/EHR, eRegulatory, or other clinical research software platforms.
• Strong organizational and documentation skills.
• Excellent English written and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to work independently and reliably in a remote environment.
• Multilingual skills are highly desirable.
What to Include in Your Application
Please specify:
• Which functional area(s) listed above match your experience.
• Number of years of relevant experience.
• A short video introducing yourself — Share what makes you a great fit beyond your resume and cover letter, and tell us why clinical research support and our company excite you.
• Clinical research systems and software you have used.
• Languages spoken and proficiency level.
• Availability (Full-Time, Part-Time, or Project-Based).
• Desired hourly rate or salary expectations.
Ready to get on our radar? Submit your application today and join the Angel City VA

Reporting to the Vice President of Revenue Cycle, the Revenue Cycle Manager will provide leadership over the day-to-day and strategic operations of the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) department. This includes managing a team of revenue cycle representative staff and being accountable for consistent quality performance, including the service’s ability to consistently meet established key performance indicators that support access and an optimal customer and patient experience. Additionally, the Revenue Cycle Manager is responsible forfollowing all revenue cycle management systems, processes, and policies, ensuring the effectiveness and efficiency of revenue cycle operations.This position interprets operational-level reports, analyzes data, and presents revenue cycle improvement opportunities to affiliate customers, as well as the Vice President of Revenue Cycle.The Revenue Cycle Manager is required to have demonstrated advanced knowledge and understanding of all aspects of billing office operations, including principles of staff management/supervision; office workflows; and billing and collection operations, including compliance requirements, as well as training and quality standards.

Essential Functions

    • Partners with CHN Customer Success team to lead RCM updates to the affiliate customer success meetings.     • Develops expert level technical knowledge of revenue, patient access, and financial verification business processes to understand how they impact revenue cycle

    • Prepares reports, analyzes data, and presents revenue cycle results to CHN leaders and affiliate administrative and clinical leaders on an established schedule through the Customer Success meetings

    • Collaborates with affiliates, providers if needed, and the central business office on process improvement opportunities. Facilitates the development and implementation of solutions

    • Provide guidance, leadership, training, and development through motivational methods to direct reports

    • Reviews standard organizational metrics and reports internal revenue cycle trends, underlying root causes, and other related issues. Applies a structured and disciplined approach to defining problems and improving performance. Champions the effectiveness of revenue cycle functional team efforts and recommends improvement strategies to enhance overall efficiency across remote teams

    • Communicates any patient account systems concerns or system issues and solicits feedback from the Revenue Cycle team to ensure they are appropriately configured and function optimally.

    • Manage and mentor a culturally diverse team, including creating and sustaining an organizational culture that fosters inclusiveness and equity

    • Creates and promotes a culture of continuous improvement

    • Ensures compliance with all CHN and affiliate policies, as well as all state and federal regulations

    • Demonstrates a commitment to CHN and Planned Parenthood’s mission related to health equity, especially centering racial equity, and deep sense of accountability to community

    • Demonstrates a commitment to learning about and enhancing practices related to racial equity and the impact of structural racism on healthcare systems

    • Bachelor’s degree in Health Care Management or Administration, or a related field, five to seven years of medical billing office experience, of which at least four years were at the management level or equivalent combination of education and/or experience

    • Demonstrated dedication to Planned Parenthood’s mission, vision, and values

    • Five years of experience with building reports, interpreting data, and developing recommendations for process improvement
