Who We Are

At Tricentis, we’re redefining what’s possible in software testing and quality engineering. Our AI-driven, codeless, and continuous testing platform empowers enterprises to accelerate innovation, deliver higher-quality releases, and transform digital velocity at scale.

Recognized as a global leader by Gartner, Forrester, and IDC, Tricentis partners with the world’s largest and most innovative companies. We’re a team of curious learners, ambitious achievers, and collaborative competitors who believe in constant growth—both for our customers and ourselves.

If you’re motivated by challenge, feedback, and the pursuit of excellence, you’ll thrive here.

About the Role

We’re looking for an accomplished and strategic Senior Account Executive to join the Tricentis Sales team in Germany to cover public sector. This role owns the growth and expansion of existing accounts plus new business, leading complex sales cycles and building trusted relationships with senior executives to connect Tricentis’ testing and automation solutions to meaningful business outcomes.

Success requires enterprise SaaS sales expertise, rigorous forecasting and pipeline management, and the ability to influence public-sector decision makers: IT service providers and federal and state IT leadership. This is an opportunity to shape account strategy, create long-term customer value, and deliver measurable revenue impact in a complex public sector environment.

What You’ll Do

  • Own and expand strategic public sector accounts by identifying new opportunities, shaping account strategy, building executive relationships, and closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals.
  • Build the partner- and multiplier-led route via ITZBund, Dataport, municipal data centers and SIs.
  • Develop a deep understanding of the Tricentis platform and translate technical capabilities into clear business value for enterprise customers.
  • Engage C-level and senior IT decisionmakers to understand strategic priorities, quantify business challenges, and align solutions to transformation goals.
  • Drive disciplined pipeline management and accurate forecasting, creating visibility into deal progress, risks, and the actions required to achieve revenue goals.
  • Partner with Pre-Sales, Customer Growth, Marketing, Partner Alliances, and other stakeholders to deliver coordinated account plans, increase customer value, and support long-term success.

Qualifications

Must Have:

  • 5+ years of enterprise software sales experience in SaaS or complex enterprise technology environments.
  • Proven success meeting or exceeding quotas in complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise sales.
  • German native speaker - most customer work and content are in German.

Nice to Have:

  • Knowledge of and/or experience with Tricentis products or comparable enterprise software platforms.
  • Experience and proven success in German Public Sector and/or experience in selling with partners.
  • Experience with public procurement: tenders and framework agreements (Vergabe, Rahmenverträge).

Skills You Bring

  • Strategic account ownership: Evidence of identifying whitespace, developing focused account plans, building executive sponsorship, and converting opportunities into sustainable growth.
  • Forecasting and pipeline discipline: Experience using data, qualification criteria, and clear next steps to improve revenue predictability and execution.
  • Executive influence and value selling: Ability to engage senior IT leaders, uncover business drivers, and connect technical solutions to strategic and financial outcomes.
  • Business and technical translation: Ability to turn complex customer challenges into quantified business impact and position Tricentis solutions against measurable outcomes.
  • Complex deal execution: Demonstrated use of structured sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC and value-based selling to navigate multi-stakeholder decisions.
  • Cross-functional execution: Experience working with Pre-Sales, Customer Growth, Marketing, and peers to strengthen account strategy and customer outcomes.
  • Sales technology fluency: Practical experience with CRM, forecasting, sales enablement, and AI tools, such as Salesforce, Clari, Outreach, or comparable platforms.

Who You Are

  • Eager to learn, willing to go the extra mile and open to AI and new tech.
  • Coachable: You actively seek feedback, apply new learning, and refine your approach based on evidence and customer insight.
  • Resilient: You maintain focus through long, complex sales cycles, adapt when conditions change, and turn setbacks into informed next steps.
  • Driven for Results: You set ambitious goals, take ownership of outcomes, and combine strategic thinking with disciplined execution.
  • Resourceful: You find practical ways through ambiguity and constraints while keeping account strategy, customer value, and scale in view.
  • Collaborative: You share information, invite expertise, and work across teams to solve customer problems and deliver shared success.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within your first six months, you can confidently articulate the value of the Tricentis platform to German public-sector stakeholders, clearly differentiating our solutions from competitors and the status quo.
  • You develop and begin executing a strategic territory plan that reflects the specific dynamics of German public-sector procurement and maximizes Tricentis’ long-term impact across the market.
  • You establish meaningful progress with two to three key public-sector multipliers, such as ITZBund, Dataport, or relevant municipal data-center hosting organizations.
  • You advance qualification and vetting processes that position Tricentis as a preferred solution for quality assurance and test automation across ministries and other public-sector entities.
  • You build an effective partner-led approach to the territory, combining MEDDPICC and value-based selling with an understanding of public tenders, award processes, and the specific decision dynamics of the German public sector.
  • You demonstrate curiosity, coachability, and adaptability by quickly building knowledge of quality engineering, the Tricentis product portfolio, and emerging technologies, including AI.

Tricentis Core Values: 

At Tricentis, we strive for success while inspiring those around us by knowing what we need to achieve and how we’ll achieve it. Our core values serve as our guiding light to drive our every action and define our ways of working so that we can create and enjoy a successful journey and reach higher heights together.

  • Demonstrate Self-Awareness: Own your strengths and limitations.
  • Finish What We Start: Do what we say we are going to do.
  • Move Fast: Create momentum and efficiency.
  • Run Towards Change: Challenge the status quo.
  • Serve Our Customers & Communities: Create a positive experience with each interaction.
  • Solve Problems Together: We win or lose as one team.
  • Think Big & Believe: Set extraordinary goals and believe you can achieve them.

Tricentis is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, gender, religious affiliation, age, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, or physical and mental disability and other statuses protected by law.

Global Sanctions Compliance

We comply with all applicable global sanctions and export control laws. Candidates must not be listed on any government restricted party lists (including OFAC SDN List and U.S. Commerce Department restricted lists) and must certify that their employment would not violate any sanctions or export control regulations. jobs.excerpt: Vill du vara med och förändra vården? Då vill vi prata med dig!
jobs.description:
Vill du vara med och förändra vården?

Då vill vi prata med dig!

Om den digitala tjänsten

Hej! Jag heter Maria Lundqvist och är verksamhetschef på Kry Digital. Jag tror på en enkel sak: vården blir bättre när vi vågar göra den annorlunda. I vår digitala tjänst jobbar vi nära varandra med hjälp av våra digitala verktyg. Det är lika självklart att be om hjälp som att komma med en ny idé. Vi är ett psykologteam på 50 medarbetare som delar samma övertygelse – att hög tillgänglighet, ny teknik och ett genuint fokus på kvalitet och patientnöjdhet inte är motsatser. Det bevisar vi varje dag.

Varför Kry?
Vi har förändrat hur vård bedrivs i Sverige i över tio år. Gjort den digital, tillgänglig och mer jämlik. Men vi är inte klara och det är poängen.På Kry tror vi att det modigaste du kan göra i vårdbranschen är att vara snäll. Och att de som kan vården ska styra den. Hos oss får du mandat att göra det - ta det, be inte om det.

Vad du faktiskt gör

I arbetet som digital psykolog på Kry ingår behandling, triagering och handläggning. Du tar emot patienter på primärvårdsnivå via videomöten samt finns som stöd via chatt till IKBT patienter. Du har stöd i form av riktlinjer, behandlingsmaterial, kollegor online samt handledning. Du genomför digitala konsultationer via vår plattform och du gör det på ett sätt som får patienter att känna sig sedda. Du samarbetar nära vårdcentralerna och övriga vårdflöden. Vi tror inte att digital och fysisk vård är varandras motpoler. De är varandras förutsättningar. Dina erfarenheter är med och formar hur vi arbetar, idag och framåt. Det kallar vi Kry-modellen.Läs mer om den här.

Vad vi förväntar oss av dig

  • Du är legitimerad psykolog med KBT-inriktning.

  • Du besitter erfarenhet från arbete inom primärvård, psykiatri eller företagshälsovård.

  • Du tar ansvar och får saker gjorda.

  • Du trivs i förändring och ser det som kul.

  • Du levererar vård med hög kvalitet och sätter patienten först.

  • Du är flytande i både svenska och engelska.

Praktiskt

Start: Vintern 2026

Ersättning:Ackordsbaserad lön/ arvode

Omfattning: flexibel % ej fast
Arbetstid:Alla dagar i veckan mellan kl 07-22

Är du redo?
Skicka din ansökan senast 31/12 2026. Vid eventuella frågor, vänligen ämnesraden "Rekrytering psykolog".

Vi ser fram emot att höra från dig!

Ta hand om dig ❤

Job Description :

The Summer 2027 UCD Reporting and Analytics Undergraduate Internship provides students with an opportunity to gain practical, hands-on experience using data, reporting, and analytics to support business decision-making within United Concordia Dental. This learning-focused internship is designed to develop the next generation of analytics professionals through direct exposure to data analysis, business reporting, performance measurement, dashboard development, and data-driven process improvement.


As a member of the Reporting and Analytics team, the intern will work alongside experienced analysts and internal business partners to help transform data into accurate, meaningful, and actionable information. Participants will gain experience collecting, preparing, organizing, and validating data; exploring trends and patterns; supporting key performance indicators (KPIs); updating recurring reports; and developing dashboards and presentations using team-approved analytical and reporting tools.


The intern will collaborate with business partners to better understand reporting needs and business questions, investigate data discrepancies, validate analytical findings, and communicate insights that support performance monitoring and operational improvement. Participants will also gain valuable exposure to the processes and controls that help ensure business reporting is accurate, timely, consistent, and reliable.


Through hands-on training, mentorship, and project-based learning, the intern will strengthen analytical, technical, communication, and problem-solving skills while developing an understanding of how reporting and analytics support business strategy and operations. jobs.description:
ICF’s Child Care and Development Technical Assistance Line of Business seeks an experienced Tribal Technical Assistance Specialist to serve as a Tribal Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Fiscal Management and Internal Controls. The Tribal Child Care Capacity Building Center (TCBC) provides high-quality training and technical assistance (TA) that improves the capacity of Tribal Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) programs that reflect the various languages and traditions that exist in Tribal cultures. The programs are geographically diverse and provide comprehensive services to children and families that are culturally responsive and respectful of Tribal sovereignty. This role will provide ongoing, prompt, and accurate programmatic assistance to federal staff and CCDF grantees with high-quality services and products that exceed expectations.

The ideal candidate will have both background and experience in Child Development or Early Childhood Education with knowledge of Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) regulations and program implementation, with a focus on Fiscal Management and Internal Controls. The role will provide support and TA to grantees by delivering training and TA activities aligned with the approved financial management and internal controls training and TA plan. The role will be responsible for the design, development, and implementation of training and TA using research-based practices that reflect the varied languages and traditions that exist in Tribal cultures.

The position is full-time and home-based with up to 25% travel required to provide technical assistance to assigned Tribes and to attend related conferences and meetings.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support client priorities and project objectives by completing required and ad hoc reports as well as other relevant information gathering tasks to demonstrate project progress and accomplishments, inform training and technical assistance (TA) efforts, and identify emerging CCDF TA needs for Tribal communities.
  • Actively participate and engage in team meetings, internal workgroups, and other collaborative projects as requested. Take and record notes during meetings, including staff meetings and federal workgroup meetings.
  • Participate in and/or lead various workgroups as requested by the client or project leadership, and as relevant to the project’s work.
  • Support digital file management, organization, archiving, and file migration.
  • Support efforts to ensure appropriate review, approval, posting, and dissemination of TA resources and announcements.
  • Assist TA Specialists and partners with training and TA planning related to Fiscal Management and Internal Controls best practices, policies, and CCDF requirements.
  • Respond to information requests from Tribal Lead Agency CCDF Administrators and their staff, client staff, national TA providers, and other interested parties regarding Tribal CCDF fiscal management TA requests, including developing an approach to address the requester’s needs.
  • Work with the client and the project team to develop a menu of responsive TA offerings on fiscal management topics for Tribal communities such as construction and major renovation, fiscal management, internal controls, program integrity and accountability, and fiscal reporting.
  • Work in coordination with the team to design, develop, and deliver training and technical assistance (TA) activities and materials that support the client's designated priorities, project objectives, and meet the unique needs of Tribal CCDF grantees and communities.
  • Work with team members to design and deliver TA events, including national and cross-regional face-to-face trainings, webinars, peer learning groups, and communities of practice, including coordinating the event production calendar and tracking logistics for events.
  • Support the development and implementation of effective communication strategies to share timely information within the project and externally.
  • Use approved tools such as Smartsheet, Mural, or AI, when appropriate, to facilitate and track task completion.
  • Serve as the content lead for TA efforts relating to Fiscal Management and Internal Controls to support all Tribal CCDF programs.
  • Support the client's designated priorities and project objectives pertaining to Fiscal Management and Internal Controls best practices and CCDF requirements to support Tribal CCDF Lead Agencies.
  • Work with project teams and TA partners to prioritize and develop and/or adapt written TA materials to meet the needs of Tribal CCDF Administrators in advancing the goals of the client and the Tribal Lead Agency.
  • Co-lead the ACF Tribal Financial Management workgroup including scheduling, developing meeting agendas, taking notes, and disseminating information.
  • Co-lead the Tribal Capacity Building Center internal fiscal management workgroup including scheduling, developing meeting agendas, taking notes, and disseminating information.

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, public policy, administration, management, or related field.

5+ years of experience

  • early education and care programs or systems, public policy implementation, administration, or grants management for programs that support Tribal children and families.
  • Tribal Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) regulations; Head Start performance standards; and applicable federal, state, Tribal, and local laws, rules, and regulations, especially related to the Tribal CCDF Plan.
  • fiscal management and internal controls requirements and best practices to support federally funded early care and education systems, including the Tribal CCDF program.
  • early childhood services working with children and families from different cultural and economic backgrounds.

3+ years of experience developing and delivering training and technical assistance (TA) for early care and education programs or systems, including consulting, presenting, and facilitating TA in Tribal communities and supporting state, territory, and Tribal child care leaders, partners, intermediaries, and providers in understanding and applying fiscal management requirements and best practices.

Proficient in MS Office Applications (Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Excel, SharePoint, Teams).

Experience with using e-learning, webinar, or virtual meeting platforms and digital work management tools (such as Smartsheet and Mural).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in early childhood education, public policy, or management.
  • Experience working within or supporting federally recognized Tribes and Tribal Nations.
  • Experience in a leadership position within a CCDF/Head Start Program or similar position and/or serving as a Tribal CCDF Administrator or Co-Administrator.
  • Experience at Tribal, state, or national level with early care and education policies, regulations, and systems, particularly the implementation of the CCDF or other state or Tribal early learning programs.
  • Experience in using instructional design, adult learning principles, and Indigenous knowledge to develop effective training and technical assistance.
  • Experience with leading collaborative workgroups to consolidate feedback, develop recommendations, or develop resources.
  • Experience providing training and technical assistance for state, Tribal, or territory early care and education systems, particularly the implementation of the CCDF or other state early learning programs.
  • Experience providing training at state, regional, or national conferences or meetings and technical assistance to individual organizations or programs.

  • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple activities simultaneously in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, while being able to meet urgent deadlines.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills to support positive client relations, team building, and business development opportunities.

Ability to adapt and learn and use new technology tools and platforms and identify ways to enhance and improve efficiency and productivity.

🏠Working pattern:Flexible working hours

We support flexibility around personal commitments while ensuring appropriate collaboration during UK and Central European working hours. You will have the autonomy to organise your working day around agreed priorities, team collaboration and key reporting deadlines.

💰 Compensation: £90,000-£110,000 per annum

📆 Start date: January 2027

Reporting to: CFO

Employment type: Permanent

Who this role is for

This role is suited to a senior finance professional who enjoys combining global technical finance expertise with commercial insight. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex IFRS reporting, consolidation, revenue recognition, budgeting and forecasting, while building effective relationships across Finance, Sales, Delivery and senior leadership.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting directly to the CFO and working closely with the Financial Controller. While the position does not initially have direct reports, it carries group-wide ownership of reporting, consolidation, planning and audit processes, with significant exposure to the CFO, Board and investors.

3 reasons to join us

  1. Purpose with international impact: Contribute to a global business helping advance precision medicine and data-driven healthcare.

  2. Visible, influential work: Partner directly with the CFO and provide financial insight used by senior leadership, the Board and investors.

  3. Autonomy with flexibility: Take ownership of group-wide finance processes in a fully remote role offering flexible hours and autonomy.

What you will do

As our next Head of Group Finance & Reporting, you will own BC Platforms’ group IFRS reporting, consolidation, budgeting and forecasting across our six entities.

  • IFRS reporting and closing:Deliver the monthly, quarterly and annual group closes on time. Own the IFRS adjustments and the local GAAP to IFRS reconciliations

  • Consolidation:Produce the group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, recharges, intercompany invoicing and agreements, transfer pricing documentation, multi-currency translation and maintenance of a common chart of accounts across entities

  • Revenue recognition:Apply the IFRS 15 five-step model to SaaS, licence, services and milestone contracts. Review new contracts and keep deferred and accrued revenue accurate

  • Budgeting and modelling:Own the annual budget and driver-based P&L and cash flow models, including downside, base-case and upside scenarios

  • Forecasting and cash management:Maintain rolling P&L and cash forecasts based on sales pipeline and delivery backlog, while monitoring liquidity and cash runway

  • Board and investor reporting:Prepare financial reporting and partner with the CFO on commentary for Board packs and investor updates, including annual ESG reporting to investors.

  • Audit:Lead audit preparation and act as the main day-to-day contact for the external auditors. Aiming for on-time sign-off with no material adjustments

What success will look like

  • Delivery of agreed objectives: Monthly, quarterly and annual closes and the group consolidation delivered to the agreed timetable.

  • Quality of outputs: Accurate board and investor reporting, and a clean audit with no material adjustments

  • Forecast accuracy: P&L and cash-flow forecasts maintained within agreed variance thresholds, with clear visibility of cash runway at all times

  • Compliance and risk management:Correct IFRS treatment, especially IFRS 15, with key judgements documented and controls maintained across all entities

  • Team contribution: Effective partnership with the Financial Controller, CFO and business stakeholders, and continuous improvement of finance processes, including through automation and AI

The strengths you’ll bring to the team

  • Fully qualified accountant, such as ACA, ACCA, CIMA or an equivalent international qualification.

  • Significant post-qualification experience in senior finance roles within multi-entity international groups reporting under IFRS, typically gained over 8 or more years.

  • Strong IFRS knowledge (IFRS 15, 16, 2, IAS 19), group consolidation, intercompany and multi-currency accounting

  • Strong experience in driver-based budgeting, forecasting and scenario modelling, supported by advanced Excel skills

  • Sound judgement, attention to detail and the ability to communicate complex financial matters clearly to finance and non-finance stakeholders.

  • Fluent written and spoken English

You’ll stand out if you have

  • Background in B2B SaaS, software or data/services businesses

  • Experience in a VC or PE-backed environment

  • Hands-on NetSuite experience, including cost centre, approval workflow and master data set-up

  • Confident, practical user of AI tools who has clearly built them into finance workflows such as reporting, analysis, reconciliations and contract reviews

  • Experience of EU or public grant financial reporting

We recognise that strong candidates may not meet every criterion listed. If you bring significant experience in group financial reporting, IFRS and planning, and believe you could make a strong contribution to the role, we encourage you to apply.

Apply now! We review applications on an ongoing basis.

To ensure a smooth and fair recruitment process, please submit your application through our careers site using the "Apply" button. Applications received by email, LinkedIn InMail, or any channel other than our careers site cannot be processed.

We look forward to learning more about you.

We are always happy to connect with talented professionals across a range of disciplines and functions, so feel free to stay in touch for future opportunities.

jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position. Also searched as: HRBP, HR Manager, People Partner, HR Generalist, Employee Relations ManagerCould you run an India exit end to end on your own, and hold your position when the person who approves it pushes back?
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Also searched as: HRBP, HR Manager, People Partner, HR Generalist, Employee Relations Manager

Could you run an India exit end to end on your own, and hold your position when the person who approves it pushes back?

On a typical day you might coach a pod lead through a performance conversation they have been avoiding in the morning, moderate ratings across two teams with their managers after lunch, and close an exit file with the payroll bureau before the end of day.

About Contour

We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture.

We have grown offshore faster than the people function behind it. This is the seat that closes that gap.

About This Role

You own the employment relationship offshore. Employee relations, exits, the performance framework, the compensation cycle, India compliance, attrition, engagement: all of it runs through you.

The boundary is clean. Line managers rate their own people; you calibrate and moderate across the org. Managers deliver their own hard conversations; you build the process behind them and never speak for someone else's manager. The VP of Global Enablement and Support approves anything where pay or level attaches, and owns org design, headcount and band architecture. The onshore Head of People and Culture holds the global standard, and you localise it for India. Everything else is yours.

Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you can run an India termination end to end, unsupervised, and produce a file that stands up without anyone checking it. Second, you can hold a position when the person who has to approve it pushes back. Most of this job is judgement carried under real exposure, and those two are the judgement.

You start with a coordinator underneath you who runs the machine: HRIS hygiene, employee queries, letters, onboarding and offboarding execution, leave exceptions, bureau liaison and audit files. You add to the team as volume justifies.

Offshore has grown past 100 people on a function that has never had a dedicated owner. Nobody here currently answers why people leave, what it costs, or whether the paperwork behind a formal process would survive scrutiny. You are the answer to all three.

We plan in six-week cycles, so ninety days is two of them, and the ramp here is one cycle rather than one quarter. By the end of month three you will have carried a formal employee relations process end to end with documentation that stands without review, calibrated a full performance cycle across the offshore org, audited and closed the India policy, Labour Codes and POSH position, delivered the first real answer on why people leave and what it costs, run the first engagement survey with the action plans owned by managers rather than by you, and got the first team events off the ground. What you build in those two cycles is the shape of this function for years.

Where the work lives

Today the stack is Zoho Recruit, with Rippling and Zoho People planned and other options still open. You arrive while that is being decided, so you get a real say in what this function ends up running on. Payroll and statutory filings sit with an external bureau, which means your job is the exposure and the judgement, not the returns. If something is wrong for the function you are building, say so and reshape it.


Requirements

What You Will Do

None of this exists as a complete function today. You are building each of the following, not maintaining it.

  • Own employee relations end to end.Investigations, grievances, conflict, and formal performance processes from the moment they leave the manager's hands. Managers run the day to day; you take over once it becomes formal, and you decide when that line has been crossed.
  • Run exits.Documentation, statutory exposure, settlement, the file. The manager builds the case and delivers the conversation, the VP approves, you run everything else.
  • Operate the performance framework.Cycle mechanics, calibration and moderation across every offshore team. Line managers rate their own people, because a rating from someone who has never seen the work is worth nothing. Your job is that a rating means the same thing in every team.
  • Run the compensation cycle.Apply the bands, hold managers to a defensible position within them, and supply the India market data that band-setting depends on. You do not set the bands, you make sure the evidence under them is real.
  • Own India compliance.Policy, the Labour Codes, POSH. The bureau files, you own the exposure, which means you know where we are exposed before an auditor tells us.
  • Answer why people leave.Attrition analysis with cost attached and changes recommended. Nobody does this today, so the first read is yours to define.
  • Run engagement.Surveys, action plans owned by the managers rather than by you, and team events that a remote team actually wants to turn up to.
  • Set the standard for your coordinator.They run the machine, you hold the standard and protect their scope, because ops work eats judgement work if you let it.

If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.

Requirements

What You Need

You should be able to point to:

  • An India termination you ran end to end: the documentation, the statutory exposure, the settlement, and the file that came out of it
  • An investigation or grievance you carried where the outcome was contested and your process held
  • A performance cycle you have operated across multiple teams, including a calibration where you moved a manager off a rating they were attached to
  • A compensation cycle you ran with bands applied, and market data you sourced and then defended in front of someone who did not like it
  • India policy and Labour Codes work you own properly, including POSH: the committee, the policy, the training, the reporting
  • Writing that survives legal reading. An investigation summary, a warning letter and an exit file each have to mean exactly one thing, because the second reader is often a lawyer
  • A position you held against someone senior and were right about, and one where you were wrong and changed it

People who can point to all of that are usually five to eight years in.

Nice to Have
  • GCC, offshore delivery centre, or multi-country people experience
  • Having stood a people function up rather than joined one already running
  • Worked with an external payroll and compliance bureau
  • Education, EdTech, or another organisation where the product is people's outcomes

The Kind of People Who Thrive Here

The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

What good looks like
  • Managers get stronger, not dependent:they run their own hard conversations, and bring you in earlier each time rather than later.
  • Nothing arrives as a surprise:compliance gaps, attrition patterns and flight risks surface from you before they surface as an event.
  • The function runs at cycle pace:decisions land inside the cycle they were raised in, not the one after.

Benefits

The practical close

Fully remote, anywhere in India. Occasional travel for team events. Compensation details shared early in the hiring process.

Apply with a CV and one paragraph on an exit or employee relations matter you ran end to end, including the point where you held a position someone senior disagreed with.

They need someone who can run those vendors, evaluate whether their contracts and scopes of work still make sense for the company, and start building the internal team and processes that let them bring the highest value work in house over time.
  • They need more control over quality, scope flexibility, and client communication than a packaged white label model can provide.
  • They need someone who can evaluate their current vendors on their merits: cost, scope, turnaround, and quality, and make a clear recommendation on each.
  • They want an internal SEO leader who can document how the work should be done, train others to do it, and build a department that integrates tightly with web development & support.
AboutThe Role
They are hiring a Director of SEO to own their SEO strategy end to end: local SEO delivery for their small business clients, their growing use of AI in search, and the relationships they currently hold with white label SEO vendors.
You will start executing and advising from week one. In the first 45 to 60 days, you will audit their current white label vendor contracts and performance, and begin identifying and building out a handful of scopes of work they can bring in house, work that either mirrors or improves on what those vendors deliver today, along with the standard operating procedures that make that work repeatable. As you prove out results and judgment, this role is built to grow into leadership over an internal SEO team.
You will also serve as the company’s internal SEO consultant on website development builds, working with their web team early in the build process so new sites launch search ready rather than getting audited and fixed after the fact. This is an advisory role on the web side. They are not asking you to manage web development vendors, only SEO vendors.
You'll Love This Job If...
  • You'd rather own outcomes than tickets; you want to be the person a shop owner's rankings live or die by, and you take that seriously.
  • You're already thinking about how AI search (AI Overviews, LLM citations, zero-click behavior) changes local SEO, and you want a place to actually test that thinking.
  • You can look at content someone else wrote and make it meaningfully better; structurally, not just line edits, without needing to write every word yourself.
  • You want a leadership track, not just a bigger workload. You're motivated by eventually building and running a team, not just doing more of the same work solo.
You'll Dislike This Job If...
  • You want a fully built department, existing SOPs, and someone checking your work daily; none of that exists yet. You're building a chunk of it.
  • You see vendor management or contract review as beneath your role. Evaluating what they are paying for and deciding what to bring in house is core to this job, not a side task.
  • You need certainty about title and comp progression on day one and the growth path is real but earned, not guaranteed on a calendar.
Core Responsibilities
White Label Vendor Oversight and Evaluation
  • Own the working relationship with the company’s current white label SEO vendors: scope, deliverables, turnaround, and quality.
  • Evaluate vendor contracts on their merits, pricing, scope of work, service levels, and exclusivity or termination terms, and provide the company with a clear recommendation on each: keep, renegotiate, or replace.
  • Within a 45 to 60 day span, identify a small set of scopes of work to begin bringing in house, ones that mirror or enhance what their vendors currently deliver, and start building the standard operating procedures that make those scopes repeatable without you personally in the loop on every account.
Local SEO Execution
  • Own Google Business Profile optimization, map pack ranking strategy, and on-page SEO for a portfolio of small-business (automotive detailing, PPF, tint) client accounts.
  • Diagnose ranking issues and build a prioritized action plan per client, not a generic checklist.
  • Track and report on local ranking movement, map pack visibility, and organic traffic using Ahrefs and other tools.
AI and Answer Engine Optimization Strategy
  • Build and evolve their point of view on how AI Overviews, LLM-based search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), and zero-click behavior affect local SEO for small businesses.
  • Translate that strategy into concrete, testable deliverables: content structure, schema/structured data, citation-worthy page formats, not just trend commentary.
  • Track algorithm and AI search changes, and proactively adjust client strategy in advance.
Content Direction & Editing
  • Direct and edit SEO content produced by writers and contractors; briefs, structure, on-page optimization, and quality control before publication.
  • Make sure content ties back to each client's actual ranking and conversion goals, not just word count.
Tools, Reporting & Communication
  • Use Ahrefs (required) for keyword research, competitor analysis, and rank tracking; comfort with Local Falcon or a similar local-rank tool is a plus.
  • Report results in plain language that a shop owner can act on; no jargon, no fluff.
  • Analyze performance trends and translate insights into actionable improvements for future campaigns.
Their Core Values
Before you apply, make sure these land for you. They don't just post values on a wall; they hire, fire, and celebrate based on them.
  • Delivering a WOW experience through service
  • Embrace and drive change
  • Create fun and a hint of weirdness
  • Be adventurous, creative, and open-minded
  • Pursue growth & learning
  • Build a positive team and family spirit
  • Create open and honest relationships built on communication
  • Be humble
  • Never be afraid to ask for help
  • Do it right, or don't do it at all.

What Success Looks LikeFirst 45 Days

  • Completed a full audit of the company’s current white label SEO vendor contracts and performance, with a clear keep, renegotiate, or replace recommendation for each.
  • Identified two to four scopes of work to begin bringing in house, chosen because they mirror or enhance what their vendors currently deliver, and started drafting the standard operating procedure for at least one of them.
  • Independently managing Google Business Profile, map pack, and on page SEO for your assigned client portfolio.
  • Embedded as SEO consultant on at least one active website development build.
First 90 Days
  • Shown measurable ranking or map pack improvement across your client portfolio.
  • Built a documented process for content briefs and editing standards that another writer could follow.
Long-Term
  • Own SEO strategy across all client accounts.
  • Help hire, train, and lead additional SEO team members as the department grows.
  • Help them settle the right long term mix of internal and vendor delivered work, informed by what the first internalized scopes of work actually prove out.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of hands-on SEO experience with demonstrable results improving local/SMB rankings (map pack position, GBP visibility, organic traffic); bring examples, not just a resume line.
  • Working knowledge of Ahrefs and or Comparable Tool: keyword research, rank tracking, competitor, and gap analysis.
  • Competence across the range of what modern SEO now covers: traditional technical and on page SEO, local map grid tracking, AI driven SEO, and answer engine optimization. You do not need to be a master of every one of these. You do need to know enough in each to direct the work, judge whether it is good, and recognize when you should bring in outside expertise or hire someone who covers a gap you do not.
  • Experience editing or directing content written by someone else, with a clear point of view on what actually makes SEO content rank and convert.
  • A genuine, current interest in AI-driven search, not just awareness that it exists.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote, contract-to-hire structure with limited existing infrastructure.
  • Proven ability to translate high-level SEO strategy into measurable business results.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain the impact of SEO to non-technical stakeholders and clients.
​Nice to Have
  • Management or team-lead experience, though we're weighing trajectory and hunger to lead over a management title you've already held.
  • Background working with local or small-business clients, ideally in a service industry.
  • Familiarity with Local Falcon, Google Search Console, or other local-rank and search-performance tools.

Benefits

  • $3800 - $6000 USD/monthly
  • 100% remote from anywhere in Latam

Job Description: Computational Physical Scientist – AI Training & Model Evaluation

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Global (Fully Remote)
Time Commitment: 15+ hours per week
Schedule: Flexible

About the Role

We are seeking experienced Computational Physical Scientists with prior professional AI-training or model-evaluation experience to contribute to a project focused on improving advanced AI systems.

You will apply your scientific expertise and programming skills to develop challenging technical tasks, evaluate AI-generated code and analyses, identify errors, and establish objective standards for accurate solutions. This opportunity is intended for professionals with substantive AI-training experience involving physical-science content.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Create realistic computational physical-science tasks that challenge advanced AI models.
  2. Develop clear task instructions, reproducible environments, reference solutions, and evaluation criteria.
  3. Evaluate AI-generated calculations, code, simulations, models, and technical deliverables.
  4. Identify invalid assumptions, numerical errors, physically impossible results, incorrect methodologies, and reproducibility failures.
  5. Assess the scientific accuracy, reliability, and completeness of model-generated outputs.
  6. Establish objective standards for evaluating computational and scientific solutions.

Required Qualifications

  1. Prior paid experience training, evaluating, benchmarking, or improving AI systems on scientific or technical tasks.
  2. Strong practical proficiency in Python.
  3. Deep expertise in at least one relevant physical-science specialization.
  4. Hands-on experience using computational methods for modeling, simulation, numerical analysis, data analysis, or reproducible research.

Relevant Specializations

  • Physics
  • Astronomy and Cosmology
  • Materials Science
  • Chemistry
  • Computational Physics
  • Computational Chemistry
  • Scientific Simulation

Public Proof of Technical Expertise

Strong applicants should be able to demonstrate their expertise through evidence such as:

  • Peer-reviewed publications or preprints involving computational methods.
  • Public simulation or scientific analysis code.
  • Google Scholar, ORCID, arXiv, or equivalent research profiles.
  • Open-source scientific software contributions.
  • Reproducible notebooks, models, datasets, or simulations.
  • Public benchmarks, experiments, or technical projects.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Experience creating AI-training tasks, reference answers, evaluation rubrics, graders, or benchmark problems.
  2. Familiarity with NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, Astropy, PyTorch, JAX, or comparable scientific tools.
  3. Experience validating simulations or models against analytical results, observations, or experimental data.
  4. Availability to begin immediately.

Application Process

  1. Application Submission: Submit your application along with details of your AI-training experience, scientific specialization, and public technical evidence.
  2. AI Interview: Complete an AI interview that includes technical and integrity checks.
  3. Hiring Manager Review: The team evaluates your profile and interview performance.
  4. Onboarding: Selected candidates complete project onboarding and begin their first assigned task.

Compensation

Compensation is output-based, with payment for tasks that meet project specifications and quality requirements. Task availability and completion time may vary.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewWho We AreBecause health is personal.  That's why Personify Health created the first and only personalized health platform—bringing health plan administration, holistic wellbeing solutions, and comprehensive care navigation together in one place.
jobs.description:
Overview

Who We Are

Because health is personal. That's why Personify Health created the first and only personalized health platform—bringing health plan administration, holistic wellbeing solutions, and comprehensive care navigation together in one place. We serve employers, health plans, and health systems with data-driven solutions that reduce costs while actually improving health outcomes. Together, our team is on a mission to empower people to lead healthier lives.

Learn even more about the work that drives us at personifyhealth.com.

Responsibilities

Ready to make the right call on care, fast, fairly, and by the book?

Why This Role Matters

Every day, members and providers are waiting on a decision that shapes what care happens next. As a Utilization Management Nurse, you’re the clinical expert who gets it right. You’ll review requests against plan language, medical policies, and evidence-based criteria, then deliver timely, compliant determinations that protect both member access and appropriate use of resources. When a case needs a deeper look, you’ll route it to the Medical Director and support appeals with clear, complete clinical summaries. Your documentation keeps us audit-ready under NCQA and URAC standards. When you deliver accurate, on-time decisions, members get the care they need and the organization earns the trust that keeps our programs strong.

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM Pacific Time, with rotating Saturday coverage as required.

What You’ll Actually Do

  • Decide with clinical rigor: Perform medical-necessity reviews and level-of-care determinations using benefit language, plan documents, medical policies, and nationally recognized evidence-based criteria such as MCG (and NCCN as applicable), in line with state and federal requirements.
  • Apply criteria consistently: Hold to policy every time, and when a request doesn’t meet criteria, route it promptly to the Medical Director for secondary clinical review and potential adverse determination per UM policy and accreditation standards.
  • Dig into the documentation: Analyze clinical records for completeness, spot risk and acuity indicators, flag inconsistencies or missing information, and start outreach or escalation right away per UM workflow.
  • Prioritize what can’t wait: Organize your workload around urgency, regulatory and accreditation time frames, and potential member impact, and raise barriers early so determinations stay timely and compliant.
  • Steer care in-network: Confirm eligibility, benefits, authorization requirements, and network status to support benefit-compliant redirection when it’s clinically appropriate.
  • Power the appeals process: Prepare clinical summaries and supporting documentation, coordinate peer-to-peer and Medical Director discussions when indicated, and route cases on time per policy, including Independent Review Organization (IRO) processes when required.
  • Document with precision: Record reviews, rationale, criteria and policy citations, communications, and outcomes accurately and in real time in designated UM systems to support quality oversight, reporting, and audit readiness.
  • Hit the standard: Meet productivity, quality, accuracy, and turnaround-time expectations, take part in calibration and quality activities, and put feedback to work in your daily practice.
  • Protect member privacy: Maintain HIPAA compliance and confidentiality using minimum-necessary standards, and complete required training and annual competencies by their deadlines.
  • Back up the team: Cross-train and provide cross-coverage to keep operations running and service-level commitments met.

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an operational and analytically driven Resupply Customer Service Manager to lead, develop, and oversee our live agent calling staff while driving client success. In this role, you will be responsible for driving front-line performance, ensuring maximum operational efficiency, and maintaining high quality standards across all Durable Medical Equipment (DME) and CPAP resupply calling campaigns. You will actively manage daily staffing metrics, oversee predictive dialer strategies, manage new client implementations, and conduct business analysis on campaign data to hit sales conversion targets while maintaining strict regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Performance

  • Manage, mentor, and motivate a team of live agents to achieve daily and weekly resupply conversion goals.
  • Drive a high-energy, performance-focused culture that balances sales success with empathetic patient care.
  • Partner directly with the QA Manager and Training Leads to identify performance gaps, refine call tactics, and ensure dynamic script compliance.

Dialer & Logistics Management

  • Oversee daily dialer operations utilizing systems such as CallShaper.
  • Analyze predictive dialer metrics, manage list penetration, and balance pacing to optimize agent active time against inbound and outbound call volume fluctuations.
  • Monitor daily agent availability and adjust staffing allocations based on lead volume and inbound call trends per campaign to ensure full list clearance.

Client Implementation & Business Analysis

  • Act as the operational point of contact for onboarding new DME clients, partnering with IT and implementation teams to map customer data and test workflow integration within the dialer and billing platforms.
  • Conduct routine data analysis on lead list quality, contact rates, and conversion outcomes by client to identify trends or bottlenecks impacting dialer efficiency.
  • Prepare and present regular operational insights and performance dashboards to clients and internal executives, detailing list penetration, conversion trends, and revenue cycle impacts.
  • Collaborate with continuous improvement leaders to evaluate dialer rules and system workflows, transitioning operations from reactive troubleshooting to proactive management.

Compliance & Process Improvement

  • Enforce strict team adherence to HIPAA, documentation standards, and data security guidelines.
  • Identify root causes of downstream billing or revenue cycle management issues stemming from agent intake errors, implementing proactive operational changes to improve first-pass claim acceptance.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Campaign Conversion Targets:Ensure the live calling team maintains a collective average baseline of 4 closed resupply orders per agent, per hour.
  • Dialer Optimization Metrics:Maintain optimal agent utilization rates by monitoring and reducing excessive wrap-up time, minimizing unapproved idle time, and managing overall Average Handle Time (AHT).
  • List Clearance Rate:Successfully manage daily lead lists and agent capacity to meet established daily or weekly campaign clearance targets per client.
  • Team Quality & Compliance Score:Maintain a net team QA evaluation score of 90% or higher across script adherence, data entry precision, and compliance metrics.
  • Implementation Timelines:Meet established go-live deadlines for new client campaigns with minimal post-launch technical or data disruption.
  • Data Integrity & First-Pass Accuracy:Reduce downstream billing and claim errors related to newly implemented client data mappings through proactive staff oversight.

Qualifications and Requirements

  • Experience:3+ years of experience in call center management or team leadership, with at least 2 years of experience conducting data analysis, campaign reporting, or operational business analysis. Experience within DME, CPAP resupply, or healthcare revenue cycle management is highly preferred.
  • Technical Proficiency:Strong working knowledge of cloud-based predictive dialers (e.g., CallShaper) and DME billing/analytics platforms (e.g., Brightree, SNAP, S3). Advanced comfort using Excel for data tracking, staffing calculations, and reporting.
  • Analytical Skills:Proven ability to translate operational metrics (pickup rates, drop rates, talk time vs. active time) into actionable coaching, dialer adjustments, and data mapping strategies.
  • Communication:Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, and conflict-resolution skills, with the ability to interface effectively with front-line agents, executive leadership, and clients.

Confidentiality:This position has regular access to Protected Health Information (PHI) and other confidential patient and client data, and requires strict adherence to HIPAA and ACU‑Serve’s privacy and data security policies.

Our vision is to enable outstanding people to create digital solutions that have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our work spans multiple therapeutic areas, including dermatology, where we engage experienced clinicians to bring indication-specific and scale-specific expertise to clinical trial programs. Our experts help ensure assessments are performed and evaluated consistently, from training and certifying site raters to centrally reviewing scores and images and identifying opportunities for remediation.

Our global team brings together clinical, scientific, operational, data, and technology expertise to solve complex challenges in clinical trials. At Cogstate, our goal is simple: to help sponsors generate high-quality, reliable data that supports confident decision-making throughout clinical development.

By joining the Cogstate Clinician Network, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute your clinical expertise to research studies around the world.

jobs.description:
Employment Type: Full-Time
Location: Remote, Lahore Pakistan

About the Role

This role is based in Lahore, Pakistan. You will own the product direction for Pixalate's fraud and privacy products: how invalid traffic (IVT) is defined and labeled, how supply chain verification is applied, the fraud datafeeds clients use to block bad traffic, and the COPPA and privacy products. You will turn what the fraud team finds in impression-level data into shipped detection, reporting and datafeeds.

You will work daily with the fraud team and engineering, and with Customer Success when a change affects what clients see in their reports and blocklists. This is a hands-on product role. You write the requirements, check the data behind them, test the results before release, and explain the change to clients and to the team.

This is not a program management role, and it is not a pure compliance or policy role. You are expected to understand how fraud works well enough to argue about a detection signal with the people who found it.


What You'll Do
  • Own the IVT taxonomy: define new IVT types, set their priority and naming, and decide how they appear in the dashboard, the API and scheduled reports alongside the legacy types.
  • Take new fraud detection from research to release: write requirements for the fraud pipeline, set the false-positive bar, run user acceptance testing and agree the rollout sequence.
  • Own supply chain object (SCO) verification: define how unauthorized and incomplete sellers are flagged, as an IVT type or a metric.
  • Own the fraud datafeeds (IP, device ID, mobile and CTV): define what belongs in each feed, the evidence rules and guardrails, and what clients should expect when a feed changes.
  • Own the COPPA and privacy products: define the classifications, reports and API modules that clients use to find child-directed and non-compliant apps, and answer client questions on how they work.
  • Estimate the client impact of every change with SQL before it ships, and plan the messaging with Customer Success.
  • Write one-pagers, requirements and release plans, and keep the roadmap current with engineering and the program team.
  • Work with the fraud team on investigations, and help turn findings into product features, client explanations and public research.

What You Bring

Required:
  • 7+ years in product management, including 3+ years on cybersecurity, fraud detection or threat intelligence products.
  • Cybersecurity experience: you have owned a security, fraud or threat detection product and can explain the signals it used and why they mattered.
  • A degree in computer science, engineering or another technical field.
  • Cambridge O Levels or A Levels, or an equivalent.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, assessed with a written exercise.
  • SQL and comfort analyzing large datasets to size the impact of a product change.
  • Working knowledge of web and network fundamentals: IP addressing, HTTP, DNS, proxies.
  • Comfortable working across time zones, with regular overlap with US business hours.
Preferred:
  • A degree from an international university.
  • Knowledge of COPPA, GDPR and other children's privacy rules, and experience turning them into product requirements.
  • Ad tech experience: programmatic, CTV and mobile advertising, SSPs and DSPs.
  • Familiarity with the MRC IVT guidelines and IAB Tech Lab standards (ads.txt, sellers.json, SupplyChain object).
  • Experience running datafeeds, blocklists or APIs as products.
  • Security certifications such as CISSP or CEH, or a CIPP privacy credential.

jobs.title: SOC Analyst (12:00–21:00 UTC)
jobs.excerpt: About the jobThe SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center.
jobs.description:
About the job

The SOC Analyst is responsible for the continuous monitoring, triage, and investigation of security events across the organization's environment, as part of a global follow-the-sun Security Operations Center. This position reports to the SOC Lead. The role goes beyond acknowledging alerts: the focus is on understanding what each alert means, investigating suspicious activity end to end, responding to real threats, and handing over cleanly between regions so that nothing is lost across shifts. The ideal candidate has solid SOC experience, a strong investigative mindset, and thrives in a fast-paced, fully remote setting where accuracy, discipline, and security are essential. Hands-on engineering experience with core security platforms is a big plus.

Responsibilities

  • Monitor, triage, and analyze security alerts and events from the organization's security stack, including SIEM, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Security Service Edge (SSE), and Web Application Firewall (WAF) platforms.

  • Investigate security incidents end to end, from initial triage through analysis, containment, eradication, and post-incident documentation, coordinating with relevant teams throughout.

  • Determine the scope, severity, and impact of security events, separating true positives from false positives and escalating confirmed incidents according to defined procedures.

  • Execute response actions within the security platforms, such as isolating endpoints, blocking indicators, disabling compromised accounts, and enforcing access restrictions.

  • Ensure structured, high-quality shift handovers across regions in the follow-the-sun model, so that open investigations, ongoing incidents, and pending actions continue seamlessly around the clock.

  • Proactively threat hunt across endpoint, network, and log data to uncover suspicious activity that existing detections may have missed, mapping findings to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

  • Provide feedback on detection quality and contribute to the tuning of SIEM correlation rules, EDR custom detections, and WAF rules to reduce noise and improve coverage.

  • Enrich investigations with threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise, attacker techniques, and emerging campaigns relevant to the organization.

  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standard operating procedures, and incident response playbooks.

  • Collaborate with IT, infrastructure, application, and security engineering teams to resolve incidents and support day-to-day operations.

  • Support vulnerability management and drive continuous improvement of the organization's overall security posture.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience as a SOC Analyst, triaging alerts and investigating security incidents in a production environment.

  • Solid working knowledge of core security technologies such as EDR, SSE, SIEM, and WAF, and of how to use them to investigate and respond to threats.

  • Hands-on experience implementing, configuring, and tuning these platforms, or writing and tuning detection content, is a big plus.

  • Experience with incident response and threat hunting, ideally with familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

  • Excellent understanding of network security, endpoint security, cloud security, and Zero Trust principles.

  • Relevant certifications such as Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, BTL1, or vendor-specific credentials are a plus.

  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.

  • Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and securely.

  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English, and the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams and across time zones.

About You

You are a hands-on security analyst who wants to understand what is really happening behind an alert, rather than only closing tickets. You dig into the data, follow the evidence, and know when and how to escalate. If you have also stood up or tuned the tools you work with, or written your own detections, even better. You are structured, reliable, and comfortable working independently in a remote, follow-the-sun team, and you take pride in leaving a clear handover for the next shift. You are curious about new threats and technologies, and you enjoy working closely with both technical teams and end users to raise the security bar across the environment.

Location: Remote — United States

Employment type: Full-time

Base salary range: $80,000 - $88,000 per year, plus performance-based incentives

The opportunity

Sensibly Sprouted is hiring a Junior Registered Dietitian Manager to build and lead a team of dietitians providing outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT). You’ll play a central role in interviewing and selecting team members, coach their development, and shape how your team delivers care.

This is a developmental management role for dietitians ready to move into formal people leadership. Prior management experience is not required.

Internally, this position is called Junior Lead. You’ll report to the Chief Dietetics Officer and have management authority from day one. The broader leadership team will support you as you handle increasingly complex team, financial, and operational decisions. Your focus is team leadership; you may provide patient care when needed, but the role has no fixed caseload.

What you’ll do

  • Take a lead role in interviewing, selecting, and onboarding dietitians as you build your team.
  • Coach and develop team members, set expectations, give feedback, and address performance concerns.
  • Progressively assume ownership of the team’s profit and loss (P&L), including revenue, expenses, and profitability, while managing retention and productive capacity with leadership support. Use financial and performance data to guide decisions.
  • Reinforce clinical, documentation, scheduling, and operational standards, partnering with Clinical Excellence on training needs.
  • Manage team workflows and priorities, involving senior leadership when decisions require their input.

What you’ll bring

  • A Registered Dietitian (RD) or Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) credential.
  • Applicable state licensure, or eligibility to obtain required licensure.
  • Demonstrated ability to coach others, lead initiatives, and improve team performance. A prior manager title is not required.
  • Sound judgment, clear communication, dependable follow-through, and comfort using performance data to guide decisions.
  • Authorization to work in the United States without employer sponsorship.

Your growth

Junior Lead provides support and feedback as you develop the judgment and independence required for Lead. After at least four quarters, you may be evaluated for advancement based on demonstrated Lead-level capability, sustained performance, and organizational need. Advancement is not automatic. Upon promotion, your base pay moves into the Lead salary range.

Benefits

Eligible team members receive medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer healthcare contributions; a 401(k) with a 3% employer non-matching contribution; paid time off and holidays; and professional development support. Sensibly Sprouted also pays required professional liability insurance, state licensure fees, and CDR registration and renewal fees where applicable.

About Sensibly Sprouted

We are a team of registered dietitians providing personalized, evidence-based nutrition counseling and Medical Nutrition Therapy. Our care emphasizes ongoing patient relationships and practical changes that fit real life.

Sensibly Sprouted is an equal opportunity employer and provides reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants.

Salary: $80,000 - $88,000 per year

jobs.title: Head of Retention
jobs.excerpt: Is this you? • You've owned retention at a subscription business where most revenue came from renewals.
jobs.description:
Is this you?

  • You've owned retention at a subscription business where most revenue came from renewals.

  • You want to own a number outright, not support the person who owns it.

  • You'd rather be handed something broken and left alone than handed a plan and asked to run it.

  • You think in weeks — though some results take two to three months to read. Waiting three meetings for a decision makes you itch.

  • If you need everyone to agree before you move, this will frustrate you.

The problem

We're good at getting people to buy. Someone watches a long video sales letter, buys a multi-bottle offer, and their first renewal comes a few weeks later. We are not good enough at what happens next — too many never take a third shipment.

Closing that gap is worth more than anything else on the marketing roadmap, and right now it belongs to nobody. It would belong to you.

What you'd own

Six measures, tracked weekly: third shipment taken, churn, take rate, failed renewals recovered, self-serve retention, and net revenue per new subscriber in the first 90 days. Five outright, one you influence.

Underneath them: every message a subscriber gets in their first 90 days, the cancel flow and the offers in it, the subscriber portal, the save rules the phone team follows, and the test roadmap. A two-person team builds what you decide to build.

Most of it you decide and tell the CMO afterward. You don't ask first. A few, like the subscription offer at checkout, you shape with the teams that run them.

What you'd be good at

  • Reporting a number you own in a bad week, without softening it

  • Finding the cause that's true rather than the one that's comfortable

  • Killing a test you designed, on the date you set before launch

  • Checking a figure against a second source before you say it

  • Pulling and checking your own numbers rather than waiting on an analyst

We're data-heavy and use AI tools daily, Claude especially. You won't build or send campaigns. Your team does.

One thing we won't ask you to do: trap people. We don't keep subscribers by making cancellation hard.

You're probably our person if

You've owned first- or second-renewal retention at a subscription business doing $50M+ or carrying 20,000+ subscribers, where most revenue came from renewals rather than new orders. You've run a cancel-and-save program end to end, managed people for three years or more, and would rather have real authority over one number than an opinion on five. Eight-plus years in retention, lifecycle or subscription roles. Supporting the owner doesn't count.

Pay and terms

$175,000 to $210,000 base depending on experience. 15% target bonus on company EBITDA. Full-time W-2, fully remote, unlimited PTO after 90 days, health and 401(k), six-month probationary period.

How this goes

A written answer, a short call, an interview on your career job by job, a 30-minute live read of a data table with no prep, a final with leadership, and reference calls. Six steps, none wasted.

If that's the job you've been waiting for someone to hand you, apply.

Company Values

We are Obsessed With What People Respond To. We are Scrappy. We are Kaizen. We Follow Through. We Give a Damn. We Win and Help Win.

Job Description Summary

The GE Aerospace’s Contracts team is a critical team member, and a trusted and proactive business partner to the product lines within the business. Contracts is the face of GE Aerospace to our US and foreign Government acquisition and airframer procurement customers. We are charged with cradle to grave contract management duties in all phases of a Program, from proposal strategy through the full development, production, and sustainment life cycle. The contracts team provides expert knowledge in customer relationships and regulations, contract terms, price, and profit negotiation, risk analysis and mitigation strategies, and scope management. As an enabler to the business Contracts collaborates across multiple functions and is laser focused on achieving a business deal ensuring both GE Aerospace and the customers’ expectations are met.

The Contracts Specialist is a dynamic role that will provide proactive contract management support on assigned programs from capture to execution and close out. This position is responsible for leading the contracts management for their assigned programs and proposals for the Defense Combat & Trainer Engines business area. This position will work within a cross-functional team to ensure flawless execution on our current programs and support the pursuit of new business. This position involves direct interfacing with internal stakeholders across the organization and externally with various Governmental customers. A comprehensive knowledge of government contract regulations and requirements is critical. The ideal candidate can develop creative and innovative solutions to complex business problems.

Job Description

Job Title

Contracts Specialist (Defense Combat & Trainer Engines)

Company Intro/About GE Aerospace

GE Aerospace is a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. Our Contracts function is a trusted and proactive business partner to product lines and serves as the face of GE Aerospace to U.S. and foreign government acquisition customers and airframer procurement organizations. From proposal strategy through development, production, and sustainment, our contracts professionals enable strong business outcomes by combining customer partnership with disciplined contract execution and compliance.

Site, Business, OR Functional Area Overview

This role sits within the GE Aerospace Contracts organization supporting the Defense Combat & Trainer Engines business area. The Contracts Specialist partners cross-functionally with program management, engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, marketing, finance, and legal to ensure “cradle-to-grave” contract execution—from early capture and proposal through negotiation, administration, change management, and closeout.

Primary location is Evendale, OH, with an additional location option in Lynn, MA.

Role Overview

The Contracts Specialist provides proactive contract management support on assigned programs and proposals from capture to execution and closeout. You will lead contract management activities for your portfolio, directly interfacing with internal stakeholders and government customers.

Success in this role requires comprehensive knowledge of government contracting regulations and requirements, the ability to lead negotiations and resolve complex issues, and the judgment to assess risk and recommend mitigations that protect both customer commitments and GE Aerospace business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Customer Contract Interface: Act as the primary interface between GE Aerospace and customers on contractual matters, ensuring clear communication and responsive support.
  • Contract Administration & Interpretation: Provide contract administration for assigned proposals and contracts, including contract interpretation, compliance support, and customer communications.
  • Negotiation Leadership: Lead negotiations on assigned proposals/contracts with minimal supervision, balancing business objectives, customer needs, and regulatory compliance.
  • Cross-Functional Integration: Partner with Manufacturing, Program Management, Marketing, Sourcing, Engineering, and Legal to align contract requirements to execution realities and resolve issues.
  • Risk Identification & Mitigation: Identify contractual risks and develop mitigation strategies; present key risks and recommended actions to senior leadership.
  • Team & Program Support: Provide support to managers and senior contract personnel on assigned contracts; assume team leadership responsibilities for assigned programs and special projects as needed.
  • Requirements Communication: Serve as liaison to functional organizations to ensure accurate understanding and execution of contractual requirements across the business.
  • Continuous Improvement & Rigor: Embrace lean practices, digital tools, and rigorous contracting discipline to improve contract processes, employee effectiveness, and customer satisfaction.
  • Travel: Travel periodically as required to support customers, negotiations, and program needs.

Required Qualifications

  • Relationship Leadership: Experience building strong relationships with internal and external customers
  • Government Contracts Expertise: Solid domain expertise in FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Items), FAR Part 15 (Contracting by Negotiation), and the DoD FAR Supplement (DFARS)
  • Influence & Communication: Strong interpersonal and leadership skills with the ability to communicate clearly, build alignment, and drive outcomes
  • Barrier Removal / Execution Discipline: Demonstrated ability to proactively identify and remove project obstacles or barriers on behalf of the team and apply learning to improve outcomes
  • Travel: Ability to travel periodically

Additional Information

The base pay range for this position is $94,000.00-134,000.00 The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 20th, 2026. GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. Summary:

  • Working knowledge of medical-legal rules and regulations that govern the confidentiality and release of medical information with the ability to interpret and implement the standards.

  • Must maintain total confidentiality of all patient records.
